claims.statement: The far darrig (fear dearg) is an Irish fairy, Red Man, in a red coat and cap; also called Rat Boys.
claims.statement_id: Far darrig (fear dearg) peri mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Lelaki Merah (Red Man), bermantel dan bertopi merah; juga Rat Boys; di Irlandia. Pelafalan Anglophone.
claims.quote: A far darrig or fear dearg is a faerie type in Irish mythology. The name far darrig is an Anglophone pronunciation of the Irish words fear dearg, meaning Red Man, as the far darrig is said to wear a red coat and cap. They are sometimes known as Rat Boys as they are said to be rather fat, have dark, hairy skin, long snouts and skinny tails.

claims.statement: Short or tall, can change size; T. Crofton Croker, Munster, 1832: about 2.5 feet, wrinkled face.
claims.statement_id: Pendek atau tinggi, dapat mengubah ukuran; T. Crofton Croker (Croaker), Munster, 1832: tinggi sekitar 2,5 kaki, wajah keriput.
claims.quote: The far derrig is generally described as short, while sometimes described as tall. It's said the far derrig has the ability to change sizes. An 1832 description from T. Crofton Croaker in Munster says the far derrig are around 2.5 feet tall with a wrinkled face, long grey hair, and a sugarloaf hat.

claims.statement: Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry: a solitary fairy with the leprechaun and clurichaun.
claims.statement_id: Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry: peri penyendiri bersama leprechaun (Leprechaun) dan clurichaun (Clurichaun).
claims.quote: According to Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry, the far darrig is classified as a solitary fairy along with the leprechaun and the clurichaun, all of whom are "most sluttish, slouching, jeering, mischievous phantoms".

claims.statement: Refusing its requests was unlucky.
claims.statement_id: Menolak permintaannya membawa sial.
claims.quote: Refusing any request from a far derrig was unlucky, as they were very imaginative in thinking of punishments.

claims.statement: Yeats: the Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, in red cap and coat, busies himself with gruesome practical joking.
claims.statement_id: Yeats: Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, bertopi dan bermantel merah, sibuk dengan lelucon keji; W. B. Yeats.
claims.quote: The Far Darrig (fear dearg), which means the Red Man, for he wears a red cap and coat, busies himself with practical joking, especially with gruesome joking.

claims.statement: He forces householders to take him in and give him the best place by the fire (coin du feu).
claims.statement_id: Ia memaksa penghuni rumah menerimanya dan memberinya tempat terbaik dekat perapian (coin du feu).
claims.quote: On dit de lui qu'il a tendance à forcer les habitants d'une maison à l'accueillir chez eux, et à lui réserver la meilleure place, au coin du feu.

claims.statement: For example, replacing babies with changelings.
claims.statement_id: Contohnya menukar bayi dengan changeling (Changeling).
claims.quote: One example of this is replacing babies with changelings.

claims.statement: Gelert is a legendary hound of a Welsh folk-tale, linked to Beddgelert (Gwynedd, North Wales); the grave was made by a hotel owner; the village is named for Saint Gelert of Celtic Christianity.
claims.statement_id: Gelert anjing legendaris kisah rakyat Wales (Welsh), Beddgelert (Gwynedd, North Wales); makam dibuat pemilik hotel abad ke-18; di Britania Raya. Wales Utara.
claims.quote: is a legendary hound in a Welsh folk-tale. He is associated with the village of Beddgelert, in Gwynedd, North Wales, whose name translates to "Gelert's grave". A grave site does exist just south of the village, but it was created by the owner of a local hotel in the late 18th century to encourage tourism.

claims.statement: Llywelyn ab Iorwerth finds his baby missing and Gelert blood-smeared, and kills him.
claims.statement_id: Llywelyn ab Iorwerth mendapati bayinya hilang dan mulut Gelert berdarah, lalu membunuhnya. Abad ke-12 atau ke-13.
claims.quote: In the 12th or 13th century the Medieval Welsh ruler Llywelyn ab Iorwerth returns from hunting to find his baby missing, the cradle overturned, and Gelert with a blood-smeared mouth. Believing the dog had attacked the child, Llywelyn draws his sword and kills Gelert.

claims.statement: A variation of the Faithful Hound motif, Aarne–Thompson 178A.
claims.statement_id: Variasi motif Faithful Hound, Aarne–Thompson 178A.
claims.quote: The story is a variation on the "Faithful Hound" folk-tale motif, which lives on as an urban legend. It is classified as Aarne–Thompson type 178A.

claims.statement: The baby is safe beside a dead wolf; Llywelyn, remorseful, buries the dog.
claims.statement_id: Bayi selamat di samping serigala mati; Llywelyn menyesal dan menguburkan anjing itu.
claims.quote: After the dog's dying yelp, Llywelyn hears the cries of his baby, unharmed under the cradle, along with a dead wolf that had been killed by Gelert protecting the child. Llywelyn is overcome with remorse and buries the dog with great ceremony

claims.statement: Gelert was a gift from King John (König Johann Ohneland) of England.
claims.statement_id: Gelert hadiah dari Raja John (König Johann Ohneland) dari Inggris (England).
claims.quote: Der Hund Gelert gehörte Fürst Llywelyn ab Iorwerth von Gwynedd, der ihn als Geschenk von König Johann Ohneland von England erhalten hatte.

claims.statement: The motif of a loyal animal hastily killed is widespread in Europe and Asia; the oldest version is from India (Indien).
claims.statement_id: Motif hewan setia yang dibunuh tergesa-gesa tersebar di Eropa, Timur, Asia; versi tertua dari India (Indien).
claims.quote: Das zugrundeliegende Sagenmotiv eines überstürzt zu Unrecht getöteten Tieres, obwohl es sich seinem Menschen gegenüber loyal verhalten hat, ist in Europa, im Orient, Süd- und Ostasien weit verbreitet. Die älteste Version stammt aus Indien.

claims.statement: The village was named for Saint Gelert of Celtic Christianity.
claims.statement_id: Desa dinamai Saint Gelert (Santo Gelert), Kekristenan Kelt (Celtic Christianity).
claims.quote: Despite the similarity, the village was named for Saint Gelert, an early saint in Celtic Christianity.

claims.statement: Gogmagog (Goemagot, Goemagog, Goëmagot, Gogmagoc) is a giant of the Matter of Britain; in Geoffrey of Monmouth's Historia Regum Britanniae a Cornish giant thrown off a cliff by Corineus, companion of Brutus of Troy.
claims.statement_id: Gogmagog (Goemagot, Goemagog, Goëmagot, Gogmagoc) raksasa Matter of Britain; Geoffrey of Monmouth, Historia Regum Britanniae: raksasa Cornwall dilempar dari tebing oleh Corineus, rekan Brutus dari Troya (Brutus of Troy); di Britania Raya. Abad ke-12.
claims.quote: was a legendary giant in the Matter of Britain. According to Geoffrey of Monmouth's Historia Regum Britanniae ("The History of The Kings of Britain", 12th century), he was a giant inhabitant of Cornwall who was thrown off a cliff during a wrestling match with Corineus (the legendary namesake of Cornwall and companion of Brutus of Troy).

claims.statement: Later tradition: descendant of Albina, the largest giant of Albion; effigies at Guildhall, London, called Gog and Magog.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi kemudian: keturunan Albina, raksasa terbesar Albion; patung di Guildhall, London (English), disebut Gog and Magog.
claims.quote: Later tradition expanded on this story, with Gogmagog described as a descendant of Albina, and the chieftain and largest of the giants found by Brutus and his men inhabiting the land of Albion. The effigies of Gogmagog and Corineus, used in English pageantry and later instituted as guardian statues at Guildhall in London, eventually earned the familiar names "Gog and Magog".

claims.statement: The name is from the biblical Gog and Magog; Peter Roberts (1811): a corruption of Cawr-Madog.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Gog dan Magog Alkitab; Peter Roberts (1811): rusakan Cawr-Madog.
claims.quote: The name Gogmagog is commonly considered to be derived from the biblical characters Gog and Magog; however, Peter Roberts, author of an 1811 English translation of the Welsh chronicle Brut Tysilio (itself a translation of Geoffrey of Monmouth's Historia Regum Britanniae), argued that it was a corruption of Cawr-Madog

claims.statement: Per the id article, Manley Pope (1862) said the name was a mis-rendering of Gawr Madoc (Madoc Agung).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel id, Manley Pope (1862) menyebut nama itu kesalahan penyebutan Gawr Madoc (Madoc Agung).
claims.quote: Nama "Gogmagog" sering dihubungkan dengan karakter Alkitab Gog dan Magog; namun Manley Pope, pengarang terjemahan Inggris 1862 dari kronik Wales Brut y Brenhinedd (karya itu sendiri merupakan terjemahan "Historia Regum Britanniae" karya Monmouth) menyatakan bahwa nama tersebut merupakan kesalahan penyebutan dari Gawr Madoc (Madoc Agung).

claims.statement: Giles's translation: Goëmagot twelve cubits tall, pulling up an oak like a hazel wand.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Giles: Goëmagot setinggi dua belas hasta, mencabut pohon ek seperti tongkat hazel; Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg.
claims.quote: Among the rest was one detestable monster, named Goëmagot, in stature twelve cubits, and of such prodigious strength that at one shake he pulled up an oak as if it had been a hazel wand.

claims.statement: Corineus hurled him into the sea; the place is Lam Goëmagot, Goëmagot's Leap.
claims.statement_id: Corineus melemparnya ke laut; tempatnya Lam Goëmagot, Lompatan Goëmagot (Goëmagot's Leap).
claims.quote: hurled down the savage monster into the sea; where falling on the sides of craggy rocks, he was torn to pieces, and coloured the waves with his blood. The place where he fell, taking its name from the giant's fall, is called Lam Goëmagot, that is, Goëmagot's Leap, to this day.

claims.statement: Goëmagot broke three of Corineus's ribs; Corineus then carried him on his shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Goëmagot mematahkan tiga rusuk Corineus, yang lalu memanggulnya.
claims.quote: broke three of his ribs, two on his right side and one on his left. At which Corineus, highly enraged, roused up his whole strength, and snatching him upon his shoulders, ran with him

claims.statement: The Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker) is a subterranean gnome-like creature of Cornish and Devon folklore; Welsh coblyn; kin to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker, English and Scottish brownie; 0.61 m tall.
claims.statement_id: Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker, AS) makhluk bawah tanah mirip gnome cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish) dan Devon; Wales (Welsh) coblyn; kerabat leprechaun Irlandia (Irish), kloker Kent (Kentish), brownie Inggris dan Skotlandia (English and Scottish); 61 cm; usil mencuri perkakas (Coblyn, Leprechaun, Brownie); di Britania dan AS.
claims.quote: The Knocker, Knacker, or Tommyknocker (US) is a mythical, subterranean, gnome-like creature in Cornish and Devon folklore. The Welsh counterpart is the coblyn. It is closely related to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker and the English and Scottish brownie. The Cornish describe the creature as a little person 2 ft 0 in (0.61 m) tall

claims.statement: Cornish miners: knockers led them to tin and knocked to warn of collapse.
claims.statement_id: Penambang Cornwall (Cornish): knocker menuntun ke urat timah, mengetuk untuk memperingatkan runtuhan.
claims.quote: Cornish miners believed that the diminutive Knockers beckoned them toward finding rich veins of tin. As miners changed from independent, family-owned operators to hired laborers for large industrialized companies, there was an increased concern for safety, reflected in the knockers' new role. They knocked on the mine walls to warn of impending collapse.

claims.statement: Generally benevolent but tricksters hiding tools and snuffing candles; like Welsh coblynau.
claims.statement_id: Umumnya baik, tetapi usil: menyembunyikan perkakas, memadamkan lilin; mirip coblynau Wales (Welsh).
claims.quote: Generally considered benevolent, they were also tricksters who would hide tools and extinguish candles. They are similar to the coblynau of Welsh miners.

claims.statement: Ghosts of Jews who mined in the 11th–12th centuries or of mine victims; miners cast pasty bites for them. (Jewish)
claims.statement_id: Arwah orang Yahudi (Jews) penambang abad ke-11/12 atau korban tambang; penambang melempar gigitan pasty. (Jewish)
claims.quote: One interpretation holds that they are mine-spirits, believed to be the ghosts of the Jews who worked the mines in the 11th and 12th centuries; another view is that they are the spirits of those killed in a mine. To show appreciation, and to avoid future peril, the miners cast the last bite of their tasty pasties into the mines for the Knockers.

claims.statement: In the 1820s Welsh and Cornish miners brought Tommyknocker tales to Pennsylvania.
claims.statement_id: 1820-an: penambang Wales dan Cornwall (Welsh, Cornish) membawa kisah Tommyknocker ke Pennsylvania; di AS.
claims.quote: In the 1820s, immigrant Welsh and Cornish miners brought tales of the Tommyknockers and their theft of unwatched items and warning knocks to western Pennsylvania.

claims.statement: The name comes from knocking (klopfen) on mine (Bergwerken) walls.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari kebiasaan mengetuk (klopfen) dinding tambang (Bergwerken).
claims.quote: Der Name leitet sich von ihrer Angewohnheit ab, an die Wände von Bergwerken zu klopfen.

claims.statement: Knockers (Knacker, Bwca, Bucca, Coblyn, Tommyknockers) are kobolds or mountain spirits (Berggeistern) of Wales or Cornwall.
claims.statement_id: Knockers (Knacker, Bwca, Bucca, Coblyn, Tommyknockers) kobold atau roh gunung (Berggeistern) di Wales atau Cornwall; Púca.
claims.quote: Knockers, auch Knacker, Bwca (walisisch), Bucca (kornisch), Coblyn (Wales), Tommyknockers (USA), ist der Name von Kobolden oder Berggeistern in Wales oder Cornwall.

claims.statement: Cornish miners brought them to Colorado, Nevada and California.
claims.statement_id: Penambang Cornwall membawa kisah ke Colorado, Nevada, California (Amerika Barat).
claims.quote: Cornish miners, much sought after in the years following the gold and silver rushes, brought them to Colorado, Nevada, and California.

claims.statement: The Lambton Worm is a legend of County Durham, North-East England, United Kingdom, set by the River Wear; adapted into pantomime and song.
claims.statement_id: Lambton Worm legenda County Durham, Inggris Timur Laut (North-East England), Britania Raya (United Kingdom), Sungai Wear (River Wear); pantomim dan lagu.
claims.quote: The Lambton Worm is a legend from County Durham in North-East England in the United Kingdom. The story takes place around the River Wear, and is one of the area's pieces of folklore, having been adapted from written and oral tradition into pantomime and song formats.

claims.statement: John Lambton, heir of the Lambton Estate, fights a giant worm (dragon) terrorising villages.
claims.statement_id: John Lambton, pewaris Lambton Estate, melawan cacing raksasa (naga) peneror desa.
claims.quote: The story revolves around John Lambton, an heir of the Lambton Estate, County Durham (in ceremonial Tyne and Wear), and his battle with a giant worm (dragon) that had been terrorising the local villages.

claims.statement: Young John Lambton missed church one Sunday to fish in the River Wear.
claims.statement_id: John Lambton muda bandel, membolos gereja hari Minggu (Sunday) untuk memancing di Sungai Wear.
claims.quote: The story states that the young John Lambton was a rebellious character who missed church one Sunday to go fishing in the River Wear. In many versions of the story, while walking to the river, or setting up his equipment, John receives warnings from an old man

claims.statement: The worm grows huge, the well turns poisonous, livestock vanish, the worm coils round a hill (Worm Hill, Fatfield) seven times.
claims.statement_id: Cacing tumbuh besar, sumur beracun, ternak hilang, cacing melilit bukit (Worm Hill, Fatfield).
claims.quote: Eventually, the worm grows extremely large and the well becomes poisonous. The villagers start to notice livestock going missing and discover that the fully-grown worm has emerged from the well and coiled itself around a local hill.

claims.statement: The witch (near Durham): spearhead-studded armour, fight in the Wear; kill the first living thing or nine generations are cursed.
claims.statement_id: Penyihir (dekat Durham): zirah bermata tombak, bertarung di Sungai Wear; bunuh makhluk pertama atau dikutuk sembilan generasi.
claims.quote: She tells him to cover his armour in spearheads and fight the worm in the River Wear, where it now spends its days wrapped around a great rock. The witch also tells John that after killing the worm he must then kill the first living thing he sees, or else his family will be cursed for nine generations and will not die in their beds.

claims.statement: The Lindwurm von Lambton is one of the best-known British dragon tales (britischen Drachensagen), with strong religious elements (religiösen Elemente).
claims.statement_id: Lindwurm von Lambton salah satu kisah naga Britania (britischen Drachensagen) paling terkenal, dengan unsur keagamaan kuat (religiösen Elemente).
claims.quote: Die Sage ist eine der bekanntesten und detailreichsten britischen Drachensagen und wird in zahlreichen Märchenbüchern, einer Oper, einem Film und einem Volkslied behandelt. Auffallend im Vergleich zu anderen Drachensagen Großbritanniens sind die starken religiösen Elemente dieser Erzählung.

claims.statement: John forgets it and joins the Crusades as penance.
claims.statement_id: John melupakannya dan ikut Perang Salib (Crusades) sebagai penebusan.
claims.quote: John then forgets about the creature and eventually grows up. As a penance for his rebellious early years, he joins the Crusades.

claims.statement: In most versions the worm wraps itself around the hill seven times.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebanyakan versi cacing melilit bukit tujuh kali.
claims.quote: In most versions of the story, the worm is large enough to wrap itself around the hill seven times.

claims.statement: He catches an eel- or lamprey-like creature with nine holes on each side of its head; thrown down a well.
claims.statement_id: Ia menangkap makhluk mirip belut atau lamprey dengan sembilan lubang di kepala; dibuang ke sumur.
claims.quote: John Lambton does not catch anything until the church service finishes, at which point he fishes out a small eel- or lamprey-like creature with nine holes on each side of its salamander-like head.

claims.statement: Les Lavandières (Midnight Washerwomen) are three old Celtic washerwomen; kannerezed noz in Brittany, Bean nighe in Gaelic; in Iberia Las Lavanderas, As lavandeiras, Les Llavanderes, Bruxas lavadeiras.
claims.statement_id: Les Lavandières (Midnight Washerwomen) tiga pencuci tua mitologi Kelt (Celtic mythology); kannerezed noz di Brittany, Bean nighe (Gaelic, Gaelik); Iberia: Las Lavanderas (Cantabria), As lavandeiras (Galicia), Les Llavanderes (Asturias), Bruxas lavadeiras (Portugal); di Spanyol dan Portugal.
claims.quote: Les Lavandières, or the Midnight Washerwomen, are three old washerwomen in Celtic mythology. Names in various Celtic languages include the kannerezed noz in Brittany and the Bean nighe in Gaelic. They can also be found in the Celtic folklore of Iberia as Las Lavanderas in Cantabria, As lavandeiras in Galicia or Les Llavanderes in Asturias, and in Portugal are known as Bruxas lavadeiras .

claims.statement: At midnight they wash shrouds for the soon-to-die (Brittany) or bloodstained clothes (Celtic myth); linked to the triple goddess of death.
claims.statement_id: Tengah malam mencuci kain kafan orang yang akan mati (Brittany) atau pakaian berdarah (Celtic); terkait dewi tiga kematian.
claims.quote: The three old women go to the water's edge at midnight to wash shrouds for those about to die, according to the myth and folklore of Brittany; or to wash the bloodstained clothing of those who are about to die, according to Celtic mythology. The Midnight Washerwomen may be related to the old Celtic tradition of the triple goddess of death and slaughter.

claims.statement: Small, green-clad, web-footed; cannard noz, night ducks (Breton folklore).
claims.statement_id: Kecil, berpakaian hijau, berkaki berselaput; cannard noz, bebek malam (Breton folklore).
claims.quote: The washerwomen are small, dressed in green and have webbed feet. Their webbed feet may be the reason they are also sometimes called the cannard noz (meaning "night ducks") in Breton folklore.

claims.statement: Many Romantic French authors wrote of them: Guy de Maupassant, Victor Hugo, George Sand.
claims.statement_id: Banyak pengarang Romantik Prancis (French) menulis tentangnya: Guy de Maupassant, Victor Hugo, George Sand.
claims.quote: An important number of Romantic French authors and poets wrote about the lavandières, from Guy de Maupassant and Victor Hugo to George Sand.

claims.statement: Breton washerwomen wash graveclothes at night, hate disturbance, break arms and drown.
claims.statement_id: Pencuci Breton mencuci kain kubur malam hari, benci diganggu; mematahkan lengan dan menenggelamkan.
claims.quote: The Breton washerwomen wash graveclothes, usually at night, under the moonlight, and are notable for their intense dislike of being disturbed, cursing those who dare to do so. They are known to ask passers-by for help in wringing clothes, breaking the arms of those who do so reluctantly and drowning those who refuse.

claims.statement: According to George Sand the lavandières de nuit are mothers cursed for killing their children.
claims.statement_id: Menurut George Sand, lavandières de nuit ibu terkutuk pembunuh anak.
claims.quote: Selon George Sand, les lavandières de nuit sont des mères qui sont maudites pour avoir tué leurs enfants

claims.statement: In the 19th century alive in Brittany and Normandy and many other regions of France.
claims.statement_id: Abad ke-19 hidup di Brittany dan Normandy serta banyak wilayah Prancis (France); Breton.
claims.quote: In the nineteenth century, the belief in night washerwomen was very present in Brittany and Normandy, but it is also attested in many other regions of France: Berry, Pyrenees, Alps, Alsace, Morvan, Creuse, Burgundy and Ariège.

claims.statement: Nechtan is an Irish figure tied to the spring at the source of the River Boyne, Nechtan's Well or the Well of Wisdom; husband of Boann; another name for Nuada.
claims.statement_id: Nechtan tokoh mitologi Irlandia (Irish), mata air sumber Sungai Boyne (River Boyne), Nechtan's Well atau Well of Wisdom; suami Boann; nama lain Nuada; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: Nechtan is a figure in Irish mythology who is associated with a spring marking the source of the River Boyne, known as Nechtan's Well or the Well of Wisdom. He was the husband of Boann, eponymous goddess of the Boyne. Nechtan is believed to be another name for Nuada.

claims.statement: Georges Dumézil: cognate with Nodens, Neptunus and Apam Napat.
claims.statement_id: Georges Dumézil: sekerabat dewa Romawi-Britania (Romano-British) Nodens, dewa Romawi (Roman) Neptunus, dewa Persia (Persian) dan Weda (Vedic) Apam Napat.
claims.quote: According to Georges Dumézil the name Nechtan is perhaps cognate with that of the Romano-British god Nodens or the Roman god called Neptunus and the Persian and Vedic gods sharing the name Apam Napat.

claims.statement: Associated with horses; in Irish interchangeable with Elcmar.
claims.statement_id: Dikaitkan dengan kuda; dalam bahasa Irlandia (Irish) dipakai bergantian dengan Elcmar.
claims.quote: Nechtan is often associated with horses. In Irish his name is used interchangeably with Elcmar -Lord of horses.

claims.statement: Only Nechtan and Flesc, Lam, Luam could visit the Tobar Segais (Well of Wisdom); the Salmon of Wisdom swam there.
claims.statement_id: Hanya Nechtan dan Flesc, Lam, Luam boleh ke Tobar Segais (Well of Wisdom); Salmon of Wisdom (Salmon of Knowledge).
claims.quote: Only Nechtan and his three cup-bearers named Flesc, Lam, and Luam were permitted to visit the Tobar Segais or "Well of Wisdom" into which nine sacred hazel trees dropped their wisdom-bearing nuts. In that well swam the Salmon of Wisdom, which ate the hazelnuts.

claims.statement: Book of Invasions: Nechtan killed Cairpre and was killed by Sigmall, Midir's grandson.
claims.statement_id: Book of Invasions: Nechtan membunuh Cairpre, dibunuh Sigmall cucu Midir.
claims.quote: In the Book of Invasions Nechtan killed Cairpre and was in turn killed by Sigmall, the grandson of Midir.

claims.statement: Nechtan (Elcmar, Der Schreckliche) is a figure of the Irish (Irlands) Mythological Cycle; probably an old water deity (Wassergottheit).
claims.statement_id: Nechtan (Elcmar, Der Schreckliche) tokoh Siklus Mitologi Irlandia (Irlands); kemungkinan dewa air (Wassergottheit).
claims.quote: auch Elcmar [ 'elkvar] („Der Schreckliche“) ist eine Sagengestalt aus dem Mythologischen Zyklus der keltischen Mythologie Irlands. Sein Name weist wahrscheinlich auf eine alte Wassergottheit hin.

claims.statement: Boand (Boann) profaned Nechtan's secret spring in the síd, drowned, and the Boyne (Fluss Boand) arose.
claims.statement_id: Boand (Boann) menodai mata air rahasia Nechtan di síd (Síd), tenggelam; lahir Sungai Boyne (Fluss Boand).
claims.quote: Diese habe die geheime Quelle Nechtans im Síd durch Herumgehen gegen den Sonnenlauf (tuaithbel) entweiht, worauf sie darin ertrunken sei. So sei der Fluss Boand (Boyne) entstanden.

claims.statement: He lived in the otherworldly Síd Nechtain, mythic form of Carbury Hill.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di Síd Nechtain, wujud mitos Carbury Hill.
claims.quote: He inhabited the otherworldly Síd Nechtain, the mythological form of Carbury Hill.

claims.statement: The shishiga (шишига, leshenka) is a female swamp or forest creature of Russian folklore like the wood-goblin; white, naked, tousled; harasses drunkards.
claims.statement_id: Shishiga (шишига, leshenka) makhluk perempuan rawa atau hutan cerita rakyat Rusia (Russian), mirip roh hutan; putih, telanjang, kusut; mengganggu pemabuk; di Rusia.
claims.quote: is a female swamp (or forest) creature similar to the wood-goblin in Russian folklore and mythology. It is described as white, nude, and tousled and is considered to harass the people and bring misfortune to the drunkards.

claims.statement: In Komi myth she lives in the Kama River combing her hair; those who see her die.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Komi ia tinggal di Sungai Kama (Kama River), menyisir rambut; yang melihatnya mati.
claims.quote: The same creature is important in the mythology of Komi people. She supposedly lives in the Kama River and often goes to the shore to comb her hair. Everybody who sees her will soon drown or die by another cause.

claims.statement: The chichiga is a small hunchbacked female being of reeds, streams and ponds.
claims.statement_id: Chichiga makhluk perempuan kecil bungkuk di alang-alang, anak sungai dan kolam.
claims.quote: On la décrit comme un petit être féminin bossu, vivant dans les roseaux, avec une préférence pour les petits ruisseaux et les étangs.

claims.statement: Per the ru article, in East Slavic (восточнославянской) myth шишига is an unclean spirit behind the stove, in the forest (леший), swamp or bathhouse; шишимора-кикимора.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ru, шишига dalam mitologi Slavia Timur (восточнославянской) roh jahat di balik tungku, hutan (леший), rawa, pemandian; шишимора-кикимора (Kikimora); mirip Leshy.
claims.quote: Шиши́га, шишо́к (муж. шиш, шишиган, шишимора-кикимора) — в восточнославянской мифологии нечистая сила, живущая за печкой, в лесу (лешачиха, леший) и на болоте (болотник), в бане (банник), в овине (овинный домовой); бес.

claims.statement: In Simbirsk province (Симбирской губернии) the devil is called Shishiga (Шишига).
claims.statement_id: Di provinsi Simbirsk (Симбирской губернии) setan disebut Shishiga (Шишига).
claims.quote: Чёрт в Симбирской губернии — Шишига.

claims.statement: Sleeping all afternoon, she appears only at dusk (crépuscule).
claims.statement_id: Tidur sepanjang siang, muncul saat senja (crépuscule).
claims.quote: Dormant tout l'après-midi, elle apparaît uniquement au crépuscule.

claims.statement: She carries off children who go too near rushing water.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa anak-anak yang terlalu dekat air deras.
claims.quote: Elle emporte aussi les enfants qui s'approchent trop près des eaux tumultueuses où ils vivaient.

claims.statement: The Dictionnaire Infernal is a demonology by Jacques Collin de Plancy, first published in 1818, listing Ukobach.
claims.statement_id: Dictionnaire Infernal (Infernal Dictionary) buku demonologi karya Jacques Collin de Plancy, terbit 1818; memuat Ukobach; di Prancis.
claims.quote: The Dictionnaire Infernal (English: "Infernal Dictionary" ) is a book on demonology, describing demons organised in hierarchies. It was written by Jacques Collin de Plancy and first published in 1818.

claims.statement: The 1863 edition had 69 illustrations by Louis Le Breton.
claims.statement_id: Edisi 1863 memuat 69 ilustrasi Louis Le Breton.
claims.quote: perhaps the most famous is the 1863 edition, which included 69 illustrations by Louis Le Breton depicting the appearances of several of the demons.

claims.statement: In the Dictionnaire Infernal (Jacques Auguste Simon Collin de Plancy) Ukobach or Urobach is a lower-order demon (demonio de orden inferior) with a flaming red body, big eyes and ears, a pan of embers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Dictionnaire Infernal (Jacques Auguste Simon Collin de Plancy), Ukobach atau Urobach iblis tingkat rendah (demonio de orden inferior), tubuh menyala merah, mata dan telinga besar, panci bara.
claims.quote: En el Dictionnaire Infernal de Jacques Auguste Simon Collin de Plancy, 181 , Ukobach o Urobach es descrito como un demonio de orden inferior. Siempre se muestra con un cuerpo llameante de color rojo, grandes ojos y oídos, y a menudo una cacerola llena de brasas o hierro caliente.

claims.statement: Inventor of fireworks (fuegos artificiales) and frying; charged by Beelzebub (Belcebú) with the oil of the infernal cauldrons (calderas infernales).
claims.statement_id: Penemu kembang api (fuegos artificiales) dan seni menggoreng; ditugasi Beelzebub (Belcebú) menjaga minyak kuali neraka (calderas infernales).
claims.quote: Se dice que es el inventor de los fuegos artificiales y del arte de freír los alimentos. Está encargado por Belcebú para mantener el "aceite en las calderas infernales"

claims.statement: Influenced by Voltaire, Collin de Plancy at first disbelieved superstition.
claims.statement_id: Dipengaruhi Voltaire, Collin de Plancy mula-mula tak percaya takhayul.
claims.quote: Influenced by Voltaire, Collin de Plancy initially did not believe in superstition.

claims.statement: Per the ja article, Louis Le Breton's (ルイ・ル・ブルトン) illustration in the 6th edition (第6版) of the Dictionnaire Infernal (地獄の辞典) shows a big head, a thin cow-like tail and a blazing frying-pan-like object.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ja, ilustrasi Louis Le Breton (ルイ・ル・ブルトン) dalam edisi ke-6 (第6版) Dictionnaire Infernal (地獄の辞典) menggambarkannya berkepala besar, berekor kurus seperti sapi, memegang semacam wajan menyala.
claims.quote: 『地獄の辞典』第6版で追加されたルイ・ル・ブルトンによる挿絵では、大きな頭に細い牛のような尾を持ち、手に燃え盛るフライパンのようなものを持った姿で描かれている。

claims.statement: The bean-nighe (Scottish Gaelic washerwoman) is a female spirit of Scottish folklore, an omen of death from the Otherworld; a type of ban-sìth (Irish bean sídhe, banshee); Les Lavandières in French.
claims.statement_id: Bean-nighe (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic: perempuan pencuci) roh perempuan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), pertanda kematian, utusan Dunia Lain (Otherworld); sejenis ban-sìth (Irish bean sídhe, banshee, Banshee); Les Lavandières (French, Prancis); nigheag, nigheag na h-ath, nigheag bheag a bhroin; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a female spirit in Scottish folklore, regarded as an omen of death and a messenger from the Otherworld. She is a type of ban-sìth (Irish: bean sídhe , anglicized as "banshee") that haunts desolate streams and washes the clothing of those who are about to die. Les Lavandières is the French word under which these "night washerwomen" are perhaps best known.

claims.statement: Seen by lonely streams washing blood from grave-clothes; can impart knowledge or grant wishes; the Washer at the Ford.
claims.statement_id: Terlihat di tepi sungai sepi mencuci darah dari kain kubur; dapat memberi pengetahuan atau mengabulkan permintaan; Washer at the Ford.
claims.quote: is seen in lonely places beside a stream or pool, washing the blood from the linen and grave-clothes of those who are about to die. Her characteristics vary depending on the locality, and differing traditions ascribe to her the powers of imparting knowledge or the granting of wishes if she is approached with caution.

claims.statement: Mnathan-nighe are spirits of women who died in childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Mnathan-nighe arwah perempuan yang mati melahirkan.
claims.quote: It is said that mnathan-nighe (the plural of bean-nighe ) are the spirits of women who died giving birth and are doomed to perform their tasks until the day their lives would have normally ended.

claims.statement: On Mull and Tiree one approaches her quietly from behind.
claims.statement_id: Di Mull dan Tiree, orang mendekatinya diam-diam dari belakang.
claims.quote: On the Isles of Mull and Tiree she was said to have unusually long breasts that interfere with her washing so she throws them over her shoulders and lets them hang down her back. Those who see her must not turn away, but quietly approach from behind so that she is not aware.

claims.statement: Irish (irische) bean sídhe and Scottish Gaelic ban-sìth come from Old Irish (Altirischen) ben síde, woman of the fairies (Frau der Feen).
claims.statement_id: Bean sídhe (irische) dan ban-sìth (schottisch-gälische) dari Irlandia Kuno (Altirischen) ben síde, perempuan peri (Frau der Feen).
claims.quote: Sowohl das irische bean sídhe als auch das schottisch-gälische ban-sìth (beide bedeuten „Frau der Sídhe“ - Feenfrau oder Friedensfrau) stammen aus dem Altirischen ben síde mit der Bedeutung „Frau der Feen“

claims.statement: One claiming to be her foster-child is given the knowledge he wants.
claims.statement_id: Yang mengaku anak susuannya diberi pengetahuan yang diinginkan.
claims.quote: He should then take hold of one of her breasts, put it in his mouth, and claim to be her foster-child (see Milk kinship). She will then impart to him whatever knowledge he desires.

claims.statement: The Beast of Dean is an English folklore animal of the Forest of Dean between the Severn and Wye, Gloucestershire, England; no scientific evidence.
claims.statement_id: Beast of Dean hewan cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore) di Forest of Dean, Severn dan Wye, Gloucestershire, Inggris (England); tanpa bukti ilmiah; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The Beast of Dean is the name of an animal from English folklore that is said to live, or to have once lived, in the Forest of Dean: a large, "ancient woodland" bounded by the rivers Severn and Wye in Gloucestershire, England. Despite several attempts to encounter, capture, or kill the beast in the early 19th century, no scientific evidence has been found

claims.statement: The tales date from the 18th or early 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya berasal dari abad ke-18 atau awal abad ke-19.
claims.quote: Folktales alleging the beast existed in the forest appear to have their origins in the 18th or early 19th century.

claims.statement: 1802: Parkend farmers hunted a boar large enough to fell trees and hedges.
claims.statement_id: 1802: petani Parkend berburu; babi hutan yang merobohkan pohon dan pagar.
claims.quote: Farmers from the village of Parkend undertook an expedition to capture and kill the creature in 1802 but did not find anything resembling the creature. The animal they were hunting was reported to be a boar large enough to fell trees and hedges.

claims.statement: Wild boar still live there; 20th–21st Century references come from cryptozoologists.
claims.statement_id: Babi hutan masih ada; rujukan abad ke-20/21 dari kriptozoolog.
claims.quote: Wild boar can still be found in the Forest of Dean to this day, but many 20th and early 21st Century references to the creature are made by "cryptozoologists"

claims.statement: 2007: the series Primeval reimagined it as a gorgonopsid.
claims.statement_id: 2007: serial Primeval menampilkannya sebagai gorgonopsid.
claims.quote: In 2007, the science-fiction television series Primeval, re-imagined the Beast of Dean as a living gorgonopsid that arrived in the present day through a wormhole leading to the Permian Period.

claims.statement: Per the bg article, Чудовището от Дийн (moose-pig) is a cryptid (криптид) of the Forest of Dean, Great Britain (Великобритания).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bg, Чудовището от Дийн (moose-pig) kriptid (криптид) di hutan Dean, Britania Raya (Великобритания).
claims.quote: Чудовището от Дийн или както още е известно "moose-pig" е криптид, за който се предполага, че живее в гората Дийн във Великобритания.

claims.statement: In Welsh myth the Cŵn Annwn (hounds of Annwn; Ci Annwn) were spectral hounds of the otherworld Annwn; tied to the Wild Hunt led by Arawn (Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed) or Gwyn ap Nudd.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Wales (Welsh), Cŵn Annwn (Hounds of Annwn; Ci Annwn) anjing hantu Annwn, dunia lain; Perburuan Liar (Wild Hunt) dipimpin Arawn (Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed, Cabang Pertama Mabinogi) atau Gwyn ap Nudd; di Britania Raya. (First Branch)
claims.quote: In Welsh mythology and folklore, Cŵn Annwn ( Welsh pronunciation: [kuːn ˈanʊn] , "hounds of Annwn"), singular Ci Annwn ( Welsh pronunciation: [kiː ˈanʊn] ), were the spectral hounds of Annwn, the otherworld of Welsh myth. They were associated with a form of the Wild Hunt, presided over by either Arawn, king of Annwn in Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed

claims.statement: In Wales they were likened to migrating geese (abwandernden Gänsen), as their night cries recall barking dogs.
claims.statement_id: Di Wales dibandingkan dengan angsa bermigrasi (abwandernden Gänsen), karena teriakannya mirip gonggongan anjing.
claims.quote: In Wales wurden sie mit abwandernden Gänsen verglichen, vermutlich weil ihr Schreien in der Nacht an bellende Hunde erinnert.

claims.statement: Their growl is loudest at a distance; their coming is a death portent.
claims.statement_id: Geraman paling keras saat jauh; kedatangan mereka pertanda kematian.
claims.quote: According to Welsh folklore, their growling is loudest when they are at a distance, and as they draw nearer, it grows softer and softer. Their coming is generally seen as a death portent.

claims.statement: Annwn is a place of plenty; Christians called them the Hounds of Hell, owned by Satan.
claims.statement_id: Annwn tempat kelimpahan; orang Kristen (Christians) menyebutnya Hounds of Hell, milik Setan (Satan).
claims.quote: The Annwn of medieval Welsh tradition is an otherworldly place of plenty and eternal youth and not a place of punishment like the Christian concept of Hell. Christians came to dub these mythical creatures as "The Hounds of Hell" or "Dogs of Hell" and theorised they were therefore owned by Satan.

claims.statement: Accompanied by Mallt-y-Nos (Matilda of the Night); also Cŵn Mamau (Hounds of the Mothers).
claims.statement_id: Ditemani Mallt-y-Nos (Matilda of the Night); juga Cŵn Mamau (Hounds of the Mothers). Matilda Malam; Anjing para Ibu.
claims.quote: The hounds are sometimes accompanied by a fearsome crone called Mallt-y-Nos, "Matilda of the Night". An alternative name in Welsh folklore is Cŵn Mamau ("Hounds of the Mothers").

claims.statement: Red ears (rote Ohren) and white ghostly bodies (weiße, gespenstische Körper).
claims.statement_id: Telinga merah (rote Ohren), tubuh putih seperti hantu (weiße, gespenstische Körper).
claims.quote: Diese Hunde haben rote Ohren und weiße, gespenstische Körper, ähnlich den übernatürlichen Kühe aus einigen irischen Sagen.

claims.statement: A hound named Drudwyn caught the wild boar (Eber) Twrch Trwyth under Mabon ap Modron.
claims.statement_id: Anjing bernama Drudwyn menangkap babi hutan (Eber) Twrch Trwyth di bawah Mabon ap Modron.
claims.quote: Einer dieser Hunde namens Drudwyn fing unter Mabon ap Modron den wilden Eber Twrch Trwyth.

claims.statement: In the Ulster Cycle of Irish myth Donn Cúailnge, the Brown Bull of Cooley, was a fertile stud bull fought over in the Táin Bó Cúailnge (Cattle Raid of Cooley).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Siklus Ulster (Ulster Cycle) mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Donn Cúailnge, Brown Bull of Cooley, banteng pejantan subur, pokok Táin Bó Cúailnge (Cattle Raid of Cooley); di Irlandia. Banteng Cokelat dari Cooley.
claims.quote: In the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology Donn Cúailnge, the Brown Bull of Cooley, was an extremely fertile stud bull over whom the Táin Bó Cúailnge (Cattle Raid of Cooley) was fought.

claims.statement: Senchán Torpéist gathered Ireland's poets; Fergus mac Róich's ghost told the Táin to Muirgen.
claims.statement_id: Senchán Torpéist mengumpulkan penyair Irlandia (Ireland); hantu Fergus mac Róich menceritakan Táin kepada Muirgen.
claims.quote: In the 6th century, the poet Senchán Torpéist gathered the poets of Ireland together to see if any of them knew the story of the Táin Bó Cúailnge, but they all only knew parts of it. His son Muirgen came to the grave of Fergus mac Róich and spoke a poem, and Fergus' ghost appeared to him and related the events of the Táin as they happened.

claims.statement: Once Friuch, swineherd of Bodb Dearg (Munster); fought Rucht (Connaught) through many forms, became worms, reborn as Donn Cuailnge and Finnbhennach (White-horned).
claims.statement_id: Semula Friuch, penggembala babi Bodb Dearg (Munster); bertarung dengan Rucht (Connaught) dalam berbagai wujud, jadi cacing, lahir kembali sebagai Donn Cuailnge dan Finnbhennach (White-horned). Connacht; Bertanduk Putih.
claims.quote: He was originally a man named Friuch, a pig-keeper, who worked for Bodb Dearg, king of the Munster sidh. He fell out with Rucht, who was a pig-keeper for Ochall Ochne, king of the Connaught sidh. The two fought, transforming into various animal and human forms, ultimately becoming two worms which were swallowed by two cows and reborn as two bulls, Donn Cuailnge and Finnbhennach ("White-horned").

claims.statement: Medb sought Donn Cuailnge because Finnbhennach made Ailill richer.
claims.statement_id: Medb ingin memiliki Donn Cuailnge karena Finnbhennach membuat Ailill lebih kaya.
claims.quote: When Medb discovered that owning Finnbhennach made Ailill richer than her, she resolved to even the account by possessing Donn Cuailnge.

claims.statement: The Brun de Cúailnge is a fabulous bull (taureau fabuleux) of Irish Celtic myth, the prize of the Táin Bó Cúailnge (Cycle d'Ulster).
claims.statement_id: Brun de Cúailnge banteng ajaib (taureau fabuleux) mitologi Kelt Irlandia, pokok Táin Bó Cúailnge (Cycle d'Ulster).
claims.quote: Le Brun de Cúailnge (« Donn Cúailnge »), dans la mythologie celtique irlandaise, est un taureau fabuleux, qui est l’enjeu d’une razzia mythique, sujet du récit Táin Bó Cúailnge du Cycle d'Ulster.

claims.statement: In Ulster a superb beast of human intelligence (intelligence humaine) belongs to Dáre son of Fiachna (Dáire).
claims.statement_id: Di Ulster ada hewan hebat berkecerdasan manusia (intelligence humaine) milik Dáre putra Fiachna (Dáire).
claims.quote: Il lui répond qu’en Ulster, un animal superbe à l’intelligence humaine appartient à Dáre, fils de Fiachna.

claims.statement: Dáire backed out; Medb raised an army and marched on Ulster.
claims.statement_id: Dáire membatalkan; Medb mengerahkan pasukan menyerbu Ulster.
claims.quote: When Dáire heard that he backed out of the deal. Medb raised an army to steal Donn, and marched on Ulster.

claims.statement: The glashtyn (Manx English glashtin, glashtan, glashan) is a Manx folklore creature: a goblin from the water, a colt, the water horse cabbyl-ushtey, or the water-bull tarroo-ushtey.
claims.statement_id: Glashtyn (Inggris Manx, Manx English: glashtin, glashtan, glashan) makhluk cerita rakyat Manx; goblin dari air, kuda muda, kuda air (Water horse, Each-uisge) cabbyl-ushtey, atau banteng air tarroo-ushtey; di Isle of Man.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature from Manx folklore. The glashtin is said to be a goblin that appears out of its aquatic habitat, to come in contact with the island folk; others claim it takes the shape of a colt, or equate it to the water horse known locally as cabbyl-ushtey. Yet another source claims the glashtin was a water-bull (tarroo-ushtey in Manx), half-bovine and half-equine.

claims.statement: Glashtin derives from Celtic glais, stream or sea.
claims.statement_id: Glashtin dari kata Kelt (Celtic) glais, sungai kecil atau laut.
claims.quote: The word glashtin is thought to derive from Celtic glais (Old Irish: glais, glaise, glas ), meaning "stream", or sometimes even the sea.

claims.statement: It chases women who escape by cutting their hem; in a modern version a rooster's crow; disguised as a handsome man, betrayed by horse-ears.
claims.statement_id: Mengejar perempuan yang lolos dengan memotong rok; dalam versi modern kokok ayam; menyamar lelaki tampan, terbongkar oleh telinga kuda.
claims.quote: Some tales or lore recount that it has pursued after women, ending in the stock motif of escape by cutting loose the skirt-hem, although in one modern version her escape is achieved by a rooster's crowing; in that tale the glashtin pretends to be a handsome man but is betrayed by his horse-ears.

claims.statement: Moore's dictionary (1924): hairy goblin, in Manx English.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Moore (1924): goblin berbulu; Inggris Manx (Manx English).
claims.quote: In the Manx English dialect, "Glashan, glashtan, glashtin" as 'hairy goblin' is the primary (and most detailed) entry given in Moore's posthumous dictionary (1924)

claims.statement: The Alastyn (Glashtyn, Cabyll-ushtey) is a humanoid of Isle of Man (île de Man) folklore that leaves the water, takes the form of a grey colt (poulain gris), and comes out only at night (nuit).
claims.statement_id: Alastyn (Glashtyn, Cabyll-ushtey) makhluk humanoid folklore Isle of Man (île de Man), keluar dari air, berwujud anak kuda kelabu (poulain gris), keluar malam (nuit).
claims.quote: L’Alastyn, aussi connu sous les noms de Glashtyn et de Cabyll-ushtey, est, dans le folklore de l'île de Man, une créature humanoïde qui sort régulièrement de l'eau et peut prendre l'apparence d'un poulain gris. Il ne sort que la nuit.

claims.statement: In human form a handsome youth with shining eyes, dark skin and curly hair; ears pointed like a horse's (cheval).
claims.statement_id: Wujud manusia: pemuda tampan, mata berkilau, kulit gelap, rambut ikal; telinga runcing seperti kuda (cheval).
claims.quote: Sous sa forme humaine, il apparait comme un très beau jeune homme avec des yeux brillants, une peau sombre et des cheveux bouclés. Il ne peut être distingué des êtres humains que par ses oreilles, qui restent pointues comme celles d'un cheval.

claims.statement: The Oilliphéist (oll great, péist worm/monster) is a sea serpent or dragon-like monster of Irish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Oilliphéist (oll besar, péist cacing/monster) ular laut atau monster mirip naga mitologi Irlandia (Irish); di Irlandia.
claims.quote: 'great' and péist 'worm, fabulous beast, monster, reptile') is a sea serpent or dragon-like monster in Irish mythology and folklore.

claims.statement: They live in Irish lakes and rivers; Sionnan, granddaughter of Manannán mac Lir, angered the Salmon of Knowledge.
claims.statement_id: Menghuni danau dan sungai Irlandia (Ireland); Sionnan cucu Manannán mac Lir membuat marah Salmon of Knowledge.
claims.quote: These monsters were believed to inhabit many lakes and rivers in Ireland and there are many legends of saints and heroes fighting them. One story has a girl named Sionnan, grand daughter of Manannán mac Lir, angered the Salmon of Knowledge by throwing stones at it.

claims.statement: An Oilliphéist carves the River Shannon when Saint Patrick comes; from Shannon Pot it carves Lough Allen.
claims.statement_id: Oilliphéist mengukir Sungai Shannon (River Shannon) saat Santo Patrick (Saint Patrick) datang; dari Shannon Pot, membentuk Lough Allen.
claims.quote: In one story, an Oilliphéist cuts the route of the River Shannon (as well as adjacent lakes) when it hears that Saint Patrick has come to drive out it and its kind. It started its journey in Shannon Pot, then carved out Lough Allen.

claims.statement: It swallows O'Rourke (Ó Ruairc), who keeps piping in its stomach, then spits him out.
claims.statement_id: Menelan O'Rourke (Ó Ruairc) yang terus bermain pipa di perutnya, lalu memuntahkannya.
claims.quote: The monster swallows O'Rourke but he survives, continuing to play the pipe inside the Oilliphéist's stomach for several days. The monster becomes so annoyed with Ó Ruairc's music that it coughs him up and spits him out.

claims.statement: Ollphéist is a group of sea monsters (monstros marinhos) with dragon, snake or insect traits in Gaelic (gaélicos) lore; Ollpiasta in the south.
claims.statement_id: Ollphéist sekelompok monster laut (monstros marinhos) bercirikan naga, ular, serangga, dalam folklore Gaelik (gaélicos); di selatan Ollpiasta.
claims.quote: Ollphéist é um grupo de monstros marinhos, por vezes descritos  com características de dragões, cobras ou mesmo de insectos, referidos como monstros nas lendas e folclore gaélicos. Chamam-se 'Ollpiasta' no sul.

claims.statement: Sometimes able to fly or speak; they live in lakes, rivers or the ocean.
claims.statement_id: Kadang dapat terbang atau berbicara; tinggal di danau, sungai, laut.
claims.quote: Por vezes possuem poderes especiais, como a virtude do voo ou da fala. Normalmente habitam lagos e, mais raramente, rios ou o oceano.

claims.statement: It devoured residents' sheep and cattle at Leitrim and Carrick-on-Shannon.
claims.statement_id: Melahap domba dan sapi penduduk Leitrim dan Carrick-on-Shannon.
claims.quote: It then went through Leitrim village and Carrick-on-Shannon, devouring the resident's sheep and cattle.

claims.statement: People near Athleague, led by the drunken piper O'Rourke, stood against it.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk Athleague melawannya dipimpin peniup pipa mabuk O'Rourke.
claims.quote: The people near Athleague were angered by the loss of their livestock and took a stand against the beast, led by a drunken piper named O'Rourke (Ó Ruairc).

claims.statement: Sea Mither (Mither of the Sea) is an Orcadian folklore being in the sea in summer, confining the nuckelavee; each spring she battles Teran.
claims.statement_id: Sea Mither (Mither of the Sea) makhluk cerita rakyat Orkney (Orcadian folklore), di laut saat musim panas, mengurung nuckelavee (Nuckelavee); setiap musim semi melawan Teran; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Sea Mither, or Mither of the Sea, is a mythical being of Orcadian folklore that lives in the sea during summer, when she confines the demonic nuckelavee to the ocean depths. Each spring she battles with her arch-enemy Teran, another spirit of Orcadian legend capable of causing severe winter storms, to gain control of the seas and the weather.

claims.statement: She defeats Teran, is exhausted, and Teran retakes control in autumn; among Orkney's oldest legends.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengalahkan Teran, kelelahan, Teran merebut kendali di musim gugur; legenda tertua Orkney.
claims.quote: Eventually Sea Mither overcomes Teran and sends him to the depths of the ocean, but the effort of keeping him confined there along with her other benevolent labours during the summer exhaust her, until in the autumn Teran takes advantage of her weakness to wrest control from her once again. Stories of the Sea Mither and Teran are among Orkney's oldest legends

claims.statement: In Shetland fishermen seek her protection from the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Di Shetland nelayan memohon perlindungan dari Iblis (Devil).
claims.quote: In Shetland, fishermen petition Sea Mither to afford them protection from the Devil.

claims.statement: Both are invisible; they fight for weeks; the Vore tullye.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya tak terlihat; bertarung berminggu-minggu.
claims.quote: Both spirits are invisible to humans. Teran is her arch-enemy and the pair fight bitterly, often for weeks as she tries to gain control.

claims.statement: Mither is the Scots variant of mother; Teran in Orkney dialect means furious anger.
claims.statement_id: Mither varian Skotlandia (Scots) untuk mother; Teran dalam dialek Orkney berarti amarah besar.
claims.quote: Mither is defined in the Dictionary of the Older Scottish Tongue as the Scots variant of "mother", which may particularly reflect oral Orcadian use. The name of her opponent, Teran, is local Orkney dialect meaning "furious anger"

claims.statement: Per the ru article, the tales of Мать моря and Teran (Теране) are among the oldest Orkney (оркнейских) legends.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ru, kisah Мать моря dan Teran (Теране) termasuk legenda Orkney (оркнейских) tertua.
claims.quote: Истории о Матери моря и Теране относятся к числу самых старых известных оркнейских легенд

claims.statement: The spring fight is called the Vore tullye (spring struggle).
claims.statement_id: Pertarungan musim semi disebut Vore tullye (spring struggle).
claims.quote: The period of the spring combat between the pair is termed the "Vore tullye" or the "spring struggle".

claims.statement: In summer she lets sea creatures breed and warms and calms the seas.
claims.statement_id: Di musim panas ia memberi makhluk laut kemampuan berkembang biak, menghangatkan dan menenangkan laut.
claims.quote: During summer months the Sea Mither also keeps the demonic nuckelavee creature confined, and undertakes benevolent labours: she empowers aquatic creatures with the ability to reproduce; warms and calms the seas

claims.statement: Telo is a Celtic god, the eponymous spirit of Toulon in the Var, god of the sacred spring.
claims.statement_id: Telo dewa Kelt (Celtic), roh pemberi nama Toulon di Var, dewa mata air suci; di Prancis.
claims.quote: Telo is a Celtic god, the eponymous spirit of Toulon in the Var. He was the deity of the sacred spring around which the ancient settlement sprang up.

claims.statement: Dedications from Périgueux; with the goddesses Sianna (3 inscriptions) and Vesunna (1).
claims.statement_id: Persembahan dari Périgueux; bersama dewi Sianna (3 prasasti) dan Vesunna (1).
claims.quote: A series of dedications to Telo come from Périgueux: on three of these Telo is invoked with another deity or deities: the goddesses Sianna (in 3 inscriptions) and Vesunna (in one inscription).

claims.statement: Télo is a Celtic god (dieu celtique), eponymous spirit of Toulon, deity of the sacred spring (source sacrée).
claims.statement_id: Télo dewa Kelt (dieu celtique), roh pemberi nama Toulon, dewa mata air suci (source sacrée).
claims.quote: Télo est un dieu celtique, l'esprit éponyme de Toulon dans le Var. Il était la divinité de la source sacrée autour duquel l'ancienne colonie fut créée.

claims.statement: On three dedications Télo is invoked with the goddess Stanna: Deo Telo et deae Stannae.
claims.statement_id: Pada tiga persembahan Périgueux, Télo dipanggil bersama dewi Stanna: Deo Telo et deae Stannae.
claims.quote: Sur trois d'entre elles, Télo est invoqué avec une autre divinité, la déesse Stanna: Deo Telo et deae Stannae

claims.statement: Consort (Parèdre) Stanna; Celtic and Gaulish (celte et gauloise) antiquity.
claims.statement_id: Pasangan (Parèdre) Stanna; zaman Kelt dan Galia (celte et gauloise).
claims.quote: Période d'origine Antiquité celte et gauloise Parèdre Stanna

claims.statement: According to the chapter, the inscription from Périgueux naming Telo and Stanna is of great interest because it mentions a temple dedicated to Telo and Stanna.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bab itu, prasasti dari Périgueux yang menyebut Telo dan Stanna penting karena menyebut adanya sebuah kuil yang dipersembahkan bagi Telo dan Stanna.
claims.quote: This inscription is of great interest, for it mentions the existence of a temple dedicated to Telo and Stanna.

claims.statement: According to the chapter, the god Telo is also known from another inscription discovered in Périgueux.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bab itu, dewa Telo juga dikenal dari prasasti lain yang ditemukan di Périgueux.
claims.quote: The god Telo is known from another inscription discovered in Périgueux.

claims.statement: According to the chapter, Telo's name survives today in the name of a village about 3 km from Périgueux, called Le Toulon, named after a nearby spring gushing from an abyss.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bab itu, nama Telo kini bertahan pada nama sebuah desa sekitar 3 km dari Périgueux bernama Le Toulon, yang diambil dari mata air di dekatnya yang memancar dari sebuah jurang.
claims.quote: Telo’s name nowadays survives in the name of a village situated 3 kms from Périgueux, called Le Toulon, which takes its name from a nearby spring gushing forth from an abyss.

claims.statement: According to the chapter, Telo must originally have been a deity presiding over water.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bab itu, Telo pada mulanya pasti dewa yang menguasai air.
claims.quote: Telo must have been originally a deity presiding over water.

claims.statement: The chapter cites Paul Aebischer that rivers and places named Toulon or Touron derive from the same root as the god's name.
claims.statement_id: Bab itu mengutip Paul Aebischer bahwa sungai dan tempat bernama Toulon atau Touron berasal dari akar yang sama dengan nama sang dewa.
claims.quote: According to Paul Aebischer, rivers and places named Toulon or Touron are derived from the same root as the name of the god.

claims.statement: According to the chapter, the archaeological context and the possible functions of Telo and Stanna in Périgueux remain undeterminable.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bab itu, konteks arkeologis dan kemungkinan fungsi Telo dan Stanna di Périgueux tidak dapat ditentukan.
claims.quote: The archaeological context and the possible functions of Telo and Stanna in Périgueux remain thus undeterminable.

claims.statement: The chapter is by Dr. Noémie Beck, Professor of Irish Studies at Concordia University.
claims.statement_id: Bab ini ditulis oleh Dr. Noémie Beck, Professor of Irish Studies di Concordia University.
claims.quote: By Dr. Noémie Beck / 12.04.2009 Professor of Irish Studies Concordia University
