claims.statement: The white dragon (Welsh Y Ddraig Wen) is a Welsh symbol of the Anglo-Saxons; earliest in the Historia Brittonum.
claims.statement_id: Naga putih (Wales/Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen) lambang mitologi Wales untuk Anglo-Saxon; tertua dalam Historia Brittonum; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The white dragon (Welsh: Y Ddraig Wen ) is a symbol associated in Welsh mythology with the Anglo-Saxons. Origin of tradition [edit] The earliest usage of the white dragon as a symbol of the Anglo-Saxons is found in the Historia Brittonum.

claims.statement: At Dinas Emrys Vortigern digs up the hill; the red dragon defeats the white; white = Saxons, red = Celtic Britons.
claims.statement_id: Di Dinas Emrys, Vortigern (raja Briton, Britons) menggali bukit; naga merah (Welsh dragon) mengalahkan naga putih; putih = Saxon (Saxons), merah = Briton (Celtic Britons).
claims.quote: The boy tells the king of the two dragons. Vortigern excavates the hill, freeing the dragons. They continue their fight and the red dragon finally defeats the white dragon. The boy tells Vortigern that the white dragon symbolises the Saxons and that the red dragon symbolises the Celtic Britons.

claims.statement: Retold by Geoffrey of Monmouth (History of the Kings of Britain, c. 1136) with the boy as Merlin; the only medieval texts using it for the English.
claims.statement_id: Diulang Geoffrey of Monmouth (History of the Kings of Britain, sekitar 1136), anak itu Merlin; satu-satunya teks abad pertengahan, lambang bangsa Inggris (English).
claims.quote: The story is repeated in Geoffrey of Monmouth's fictional History of the Kings of Britain (c. 1136). In this telling the boy is identified as the young Merlin. The Historia Brittonum and History of the Kings of Britain are the only medieval texts to use the white dragon as a symbol of the English.

claims.statement: A similar story in Lludd and Llefelys, without Briton or Saxon meaning.
claims.statement_id: Kisah serupa dalam Lludd and Llefelys, tanpa makna Briton (Britons) atau Saxon (Saxons).
claims.quote: A similar story of white and red dragons fighting is found in the medieval romance Lludd and Llefelys, although in this case the dragons are not used to symbolize Britons or Saxons.

claims.statement: Giles's translation of Nennius: the white serpent is the dragon of the people occupying Britain; the red is the king's.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Giles atas Nennius: ular putih naga bangsa yang menduduki Britania (Britain); ular merah naga raja.
claims.quote: the two serpents are two dragons; the red serpent is your dragon, but the white serpent is the dragon of the people who occupy several provinces and districts of Britain, even almost from sea to sea

claims.statement: Merlin's prophecy (Giles): woe to the red dragon; the white dragon signifies the Saxons.
claims.statement_id: Nubuat Merlin (Old English Chronicles, Gutenberg; Giles): celakalah naga merah (Woe to the red dragon); naga putih melambangkan Saxon (Saxons).
claims.quote: "Woe to the red dragon, for his banishment hasteneth on. His lurking holes shall be seized by the white dragon, which signifies the Saxons whom you invited over; but the red denotes the British nation, which shall be oppressed by the white.

claims.statement: Cath Palug (Palug's Cat) was a monstrous cat of Welsh myth, born in Gwynedd to Henwen of Cornwall, haunting Anglesey until Kay hunted it; elsewhere its foe is King Arthur or Ogier the Dane.
claims.statement_id: Cath Palug (Cath Paluc, Cath Balug, Cath Balwg; Kucing Palug) kucing raksasa mitologi Wales (Welsh), legenda Arthurian; lahir di Gwynedd dari Henwen dari Cornwall; menghantui Anglesey (Isle of Anglesey) sampai Kay memburunya; di luar Wales lawannya Raja Arthur (King Arthur) atau Ogier the Dane; Chapalu (French, Prancis); di Britania dan Prancis.
claims.quote: was a monstrous cat in Welsh mythology associated with Arthurian legend. Given birth to in Gwynedd by the pig Henwen of Cornwall, the cat was to haunt the Isle of Anglesey until Kay went to the island to hunt it down. Outside of Wales, the cat's opponent has been transposed to King Arthur himself or, occasionally, other legendary heroes such as Ogier the Dane.

claims.statement: Chapalu (French) = chat cat + palu bog, the bog cat.
claims.statement_id: Chapalu (Prancis, French) = chat kucing + palu rawa, kucing rawa; nama Wales mungkin kucing pencakar.
claims.quote: Chapalu , the French form can be broken down into chat 'cat' + palu 'bog', hence 'the bog cat'.

claims.statement: Always near water: Lac du Bourget, Lake Geneva in France, or the sea in Wales.
claims.statement_id: Selalu dekat air: Lac du Bourget, Danau Jenewa (Lake Geneva), Prancis (France), atau laut di Wales.
claims.quote: Cath Palug is always localised near water, such as the lakes of Lac du Bourget and Lake Geneva in France (cf. also § Local lore), or the sea in Wales.

claims.statement: Welsh Triads: born to Henwen at Llanfair, cast into the sea, crossed the Menai Strait to Anglesey (Ynys Môn), raised by Palug's sons; one of the island's three plagues.
claims.statement_id: Welsh Triads: lahir dari Henwen di Llanfair, dibuang ke laut, menyeberangi Selat Menai (Menai Strait) ke Anglesey (Ynys Môn), dibesarkan putra Palug; tiga wabah pulau.
claims.quote: According to this source, it started life as a kitten (lit "whelp" ), given birth by the great white sow Henwen at the black rock in Llanfair [cy]. There the kitten was cast into the sea, but it crossed the Menai Strait and was found on Ynys Môn (Anglesey), where the sons of Palug raised it, not realizing the cat was to become one of the three great plagues of the island.

claims.statement: Chapalu (Capalu, Capalus) is a monstrous cat (chat monstrueux) in medieval French (français) Arthurian manuscripts.
claims.statement_id: Chapalu (Capalu, Capalus) kucing raksasa (chat monstrueux) dalam naskah abad pertengahan Prancis (français) legenda Arthurian.
claims.quote: Le Chapalu, Capalu ou Capalus est un chat monstrueux dont parlent des manuscrits médiévaux français rattachés à la légende arthurienne.

claims.statement: La Bataille Loquifer: Chapalu is born of the fairy (fée) Brunehaut and seeks to be human again; texts and a mosaic show King Arthur (roi Arthur) fighting it.
claims.statement_id: La Bataille Loquifer: Chapalu lahir dari peri (fée) Brunehaut, ingin kembali manusia; mosaik dan teks: pertarungan Raja Arthur (roi Arthur).
claims.quote: Selon La Bataille Loquifer, le Chapalu est le fruit du viol de la fée Brunehaut par le luiton Gringalet et, maudit par sa naissance, cherche à redevenir humain. Quelques textes ainsi qu'une mosaïque attestent d'un combat du roi Arthur contre lui.

claims.statement: In the Old Welsh poem Pa Gur in the Black Book of Carmarthen, Cai (Kay) slew it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi Wales Kuno (Old Welsh) Pa Gur, Black Book of Carmarthen, Cai (Kay) membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Cath Palug was fought and slain by Cai (Kay), or so it is implied, in the incomplete Old Welsh poem Pa Gur yv y Porthaur found in the Llyfr Du Caerfyrddin (The Black Book of Carmarthen, written before 1250).

claims.statement: The ceffyl dŵr (ceffyl dwfr) is a Welsh water horse, counterpart of the Scottish kelpie, compared with the Irish púca, each uisge and the Manx glaistyn.
claims.statement_id: Ceffyl Dŵr (ceffyl dwfr) kuda air cerita rakyat Wales (Welsh), padanan kelpie (Kelpie) Skotlandia (Scottish), dibandingkan púca Irlandia (Irish), each uisge (Each-uisge), glaistyn Manx (Glashtyn); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a water horse in Welsh folklore. It is most commonly considered a counterpart to the Scottish kelpie, but has also been compared to the Irish púca, the Irish and Scottish each uisge, and the Manx glaistyn.

claims.statement: Lives in mountain pools and waterfalls; a spirit as a grey or black white-maned horse, sometimes winged.
claims.statement_id: Menghuni kolam gunung dan air terjun; roh berwujud kuda kelabu atau hitam bersurai putih, kadang bersayap.
claims.quote: The ceffyl dŵr is said to inhabit mostly mountain pools and waterfalls, though it has been known to frequent rivers and seashores as well. It was believed to be a spirit assuming the shape of a horse, usually grey or black with a white mane, sometimes glowing or winged, to entice unwary travellers to ride him.

claims.statement: Carries the rider far or flies and evaporates, dropping the rider to death.
claims.statement_id: Membawa penunggang jauh atau terbang lalu menguap, menjatuhkannya hingga tewas.
claims.quote: Once mounted it would either carry its rider great distances very quickly, or fly into the sky, then evaporate into air or mist, dropping the unfortunate rider to their death.

claims.statement: In North Wales malevolent with fiery eyes; in South Wales more positive.
claims.statement_id: Di Wales Utara (North Wales) jahat bermata api; di Wales Selatan (South Wales) lebih baik.
claims.quote: In North Wales he was often seen as malevolent, described with fiery eyes and a dark, forbidding presence, whereas in South Wales he was generally more positively seen as, at worst, a pest to travellers, and at best a great aid to tired travellers and often luminescent.

claims.statement: It became a goat charging people, or a frog in the Vale of Clwyd that choked people.
claims.statement_id: Berubah menjadi kambing yang menyeruduk atau katak di Vale of Clwyd yang mencekik orang.
claims.quote: Sometimes it took the form of a goat and charged at people with enough force to cause serious injury. In the Vale of Clwyd a ceffyl dŵr often transformed into a frog which hopped on people's backs and choked them.

claims.statement: Ceffyl dŵr means water horse (Wasserpferd); kin to the each uisge and Kelpie but less vicious.
claims.statement_id: Ceffyl dŵr berarti kuda air (Wasserpferd); kerabat each uisge dan Kelpie, tapi tak sejahat mereka.
claims.quote: Ceffyl dŵr bedeutet wörtlich aus dem Walisischen übersetzt „Wasserpferd“ (ceffyl – Pferd und dŵr – Wasser). Es ist verwandt mit den anderen weitverbreiteten Wasserpferden in der keltischen Mythologie wie dem each uisge (so die schottisch-gälische Namensform, irisch-gälisch each uisce, anglisierte irische Form aughisky) oder dem Kelpie, aber nicht so bösartig wie diese.

claims.statement: Fuath (Scottish Gaelic, hatred; fuathan) is a class of malevolent spirits of Scottish Highland and Irish folklore, especially water spirits.
claims.statement_id: Fuath (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic, kebencian; fuathan) golongan roh jahat cerita rakyat Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highland) dan Irlandia (Irish Folklore), terutama roh air; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a class of malevolent spirits in Scottish Highland folklore and Irish Folklore especially water spirits.

claims.statement: At Moulin na Vaugha (Sutherland) a fuath was a noseless yellow-haired banshee in green silk; subdued by steel; became a jellyfish-like mass in light; her son the brollachan.
claims.statement_id: Di Moulin na Vaugha (Sutherland), fuath banshee tanpa hidung berambut kuning bergaun sutra hijau; ditundukkan dengan baja; menjadi gumpalan saat disinari.
claims.quote: A fuath once seen at this mill was a nose-less banshee with yellow hair wearing a green silk dress; in the story of its capture it was tormented into submission by use of steel (awl, and more effectively by a sewing needle), but it turned to a jellyfish-like mass when light was shone on it.

claims.statement: A general class of spirits of sea, rivers, fresh water and sea lochs.
claims.statement_id: Golongan umum roh laut, sungai, air tawar, loch laut.
claims.quote: The term "fuath" has been explained to be a generic class of spirits inhabiting the sea, rivers, fresh water, or sea lochs, with several "subspecies" falling under it.

claims.statement: Fuath means hatred, from Old Irish fúath; also ghost; also called arrachd or fuath-arrachd.
claims.statement_id: Fuath berarti kebencian, dari Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish) fúath; juga hantu; nama lain arrachd, fuath-arrachd.
claims.quote: The Scottish Gaelic term fuath has been explained to mean 'hatred' or 'aversion', derived from Old Irish fúath 'hate, likeness'. The term is also glossed to mean 'ghost' or 'spectre'. An alternative name for this class of monsters is the arrachd or fuath-arrachd.

claims.statement: They intermarry with humans; offspring grow a mane and tail.
claims.statement_id: Kawin dengan manusia; keturunan bersurai dan berekor.
claims.quote: They sometimes reputedly intermarry with human beings (typically the female), whose offspring develop a mane and tail.

claims.statement: Fuath is a malicious Gaelic water spirit (bösartiger, gälischer Wassergeist); the name is also used for the Kelpie, Each Uisge or Bean-Nighe.
claims.statement_id: Fuath roh air Gaelik jahat (bösartiger, gälischer Wassergeist); nama juga untuk Kelpie, Each Uisge, Bean-Nighe.
claims.quote: ist ein bösartiger, gälischer Wassergeist. Der Name wird regional auch manchmal für das Kelpie oder das Each Uisge in Nordirland oder der Bean-Nighe verwendet.

claims.statement: Shaggy yellow fur (gelben Fell) or a mane; webbed toes, spiked tail, no nose; wear green (Grün), the fairies' (Feen) colour.
claims.statement_id: Bulu kuning lebat (gelben Fell) atau surai; jari kaki berselaput, ekor berduri, tanpa hidung; berpakaian hijau (Grün), warna peri (Feen).
claims.quote: In manchen Beschreibungen sind sie bedeckt mit einem zottigen, gelben Fell, in anderen haben sie nur eine lange Mähne entlang ihrem Rücken. Sie haben Schwimmhäute zwischen den Zehen, einen Schwanz mit Stacheln und keine Nase. Sie tragen für gewöhnlich Grün, die Farbe der Feen

claims.statement: Moulin na Vaugha (Mill of the Fuath) in Sutherland was haunted by a fuath and her son the brollachan.
claims.statement_id: Moulin na Vaugha (Penggilingan Fuath) di Sutherland dihantui fuath dan putranya brollachan (Brollachan).
claims.quote: In Sutherland was the so-called Moulin na Vaugha/Fouadh, ‘Mill of the Fuath', haunted by the fuath and her son, the amorphous brollachan.

claims.statement: Henwen (Old White) is a sow of Welsh legend who per the Welsh Triads bore Cath Palug, fought by Cai (Sir Kay) or King Arthur.
claims.statement_id: Henwen (Old White, Si Tua Putih) babi betina legenda Wales (Welsh), menurut Welsh Triads ibu Cath Palug yang dilawan Cai (Sir Kay) atau Raja Arthur (King Arthur); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Henwen, meaning "Old White", is in Welsh legend a sow (female pig) which according to the Welsh Triads gave birth to Cath Palug, a monstrous cat depicted as combating with either Cai (Sir Kay) or King Arthur of Arthurian Legends.

claims.statement: Three Powerful Swineherds of the Isle of Britain: kept by Coll son of Collfrewy for Dallwyr Dallben; the Glen of Dallwyr in Cornwall.
claims.statement_id: Three Powerful Swineherds of the Isle of Britain: dipelihara Coll putra Collfrewy untuk Dallwyr Dallben; Lembah Dallwyr (Glen of Dallwyr), Cornwall.
claims.quote: According to the triad "Three Powerful Swineherds of the Isle of Britain", the sow was kept by one Coll, son of Collfrewy, a pigkeeper for Dallwyr Dallben (also spelt Dallweir). The variant Red Book of Hergest (RBH) and White Book of Rhydderch (WBR) texts add that the Dallwyr held a valley named after him, the Glen of Dallwyr in Cornwall.

claims.statement: Her birthing boded ill for the Isle of Britain; chased into the sea at Penrhyn Awstin, she re-emerged at Aber Tarogi, Gwent Is-coed.
claims.statement_id: Kelahirannya pertanda buruk bagi Pulau Britania (Isle of Britain); dikejar ke laut di Penrhyn Awstin, muncul di Aber Tarogi, Gwent Is-coed.
claims.quote: The sow was ready to give birth, but this boded ill for the Isle of Britain, according to prophecy, so she was chased until she plunged into the sea at Penrhyn Awstin in Cornwall. The sow eventually re-emerges on land at Aber Tarogi in Gwent Is-coed (a subdivision of Gwent).

claims.statement: At Maes Gwenith (Wheat Field) in Gwent a grain of wheat and a bee; at Llonion barley and a bee.
claims.statement_id: Di Maes Gwenith (Wheat Field), Gwent: gandum dan lebah; di Llonion: jelai dan lebah.
claims.quote: At Wheat Field (Maes Gwenith) in Gwent, a grain of wheat and a bee At Llonion in Pembroke/Dyfed, a grain of barley and a bee

claims.statement: Don Carleton: an allegory of Arthur harrying a female religious leader.
claims.statement_id: Don Carleton: alegori perburuan Arthur terhadap pemimpin agama perempuan.
claims.quote: Don Carleton suggests that the tale of Henwen is an allegorical account of the harrying of a female religious leader across south-west Britain by Arthur.

claims.statement: Henwen (Vieille Blanche; Ancêtre Sacrée) is a fabulous sow (truie fabuleuse) of Arthurian legend born in Wales (Pays de Galles). (Sacred Ancestor)
claims.statement_id: Henwen (Vieille Blanche; Ancêtre Sacrée, Leluhur Suci) babi betina ajaib (truie fabuleuse) legenda Arthurian, lahir di Wales (Pays de Galles); Hen Wen. (Sacred Ancestor)
claims.quote: Henwen (« la Vieille Blanche », « l'Ancêtre Sacrée ») est, dans la légende arthurienne, une truie fabuleuse, née au Pays de Galles.

claims.statement: At the Hill of Cyferthwch in Snowdonia a wolf-cub and eaglet; at Llanfair in Arfon under the Black Rock a kitten.
claims.statement_id: Di bukit Cyferthwch, Snowdonia: anak serigala dan anak elang; di Llanfair, Arfon, di bawah Batu Hitam: anak kucing.
claims.quote: At the Hill of Cyferthwch in Snowdonia (Eryri); a wolf-cub and eaglet At Llanfair in Arfon under the Black Rock (Maen Du), a kitten.

claims.statement: The kitten was cast into the Menai Strait and raised by Palug's sons on Anglesey as Cath Palug.
claims.statement_id: Anak kucing dibuang ke Selat Menai, dibesarkan putra Palug di Anglesey menjadi Cath Palug.
claims.quote: The swineherd took the kitten and cast in into the Menai Strait. Then on the isle of Anglesey (Welsh: Ynys Môn ; or Mona), which is across the strait, the sons of Palug reared the cat which became the Cath Palug.

claims.statement: She brings barley (orge) and rye (seigle) to Wales or gives birth to the Chat Palug.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa jelai (orge) dan gandum hitam (seigle) ke Wales atau melahirkan Chat Palug.
claims.quote: elle s'échappe dans la mer en revenant périodiquement sur la côte pour apporter l'orge et le seigle au Pays de Galles, ou accoucher du Chat Palug.

claims.statement: In Celtic polytheism Latis names two deities of Roman Britain: Dea Latis and Deus Latis, one inscription each.
claims.statement_id: Dalam politeisme Kelt (Celtic), Latis nama dua dewa di Britania Romawi (Roman Britain): Dea Latis dan Deus Latis, satu prasasti masing-masing; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: In ancient Celtic polytheism, Latis is the name of two Celtic deities worshipped in Roman Britain. One is a goddess (Dea Latis), the other a god (Deus Latis), and they are both known from a single inscription each.

claims.statement: The Dea Latis dedication at Birdoswald Roman Fort, Cumbria, England, 1873: DIE LATI.
claims.statement_id: Persembahan Dea Latis di Birdoswald Roman Fort, Cumbria, Inggris (England), 1873: DIE LATI.
claims.quote: The dedication to Dea Latis was found at Birdoswald Roman Fort in Cumbria, England, in 1873. It reads simply: DIE LATI For the goddess Latis.

claims.statement: The stone is in the Carlisle Museum; perhaps linked with nearby rivers.
claims.statement_id: Batu di Carlisle Museum; mungkin dikaitkan dengan sungai.
claims.quote: The stone is now in the Carlisle Museum. She may have been associated with the nearby rivers.

claims.statement: The Deus Latis altar (DEO LATI LVCIVS VRSEI) at Aballava, Burgh-by-Sands, lay near a horned god and a dedication to Belatucadros.
claims.statement_id: Altar Deus Latis ditemukan dekat gambar dewa bertanduk dan persembahan untuk Belatucadros.
claims.quote: The altar-stone to Deus Latis was found near an image of a horned god and another dedication to the god Belatucadros.

claims.statement: The name may relate to Proto-Celtic *lati- liquor, *lat- day, or *lāto- lust.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Proto-Kelt (Proto-Celtic) *lati- minuman keras, *lat- hari, *lāto- nafsu.
claims.quote: The name 'Latis' may conceivably be related to the Proto-Celtic words *lati- meaning 'liquor', *lat- 'day', or *lāto- 'lust'.

claims.statement: Latis is known as goddess of water and beer (déesse de l'eau et de la bière).
claims.statement_id: Latis dewi air dan bir (déesse de l'eau et de la bière).
claims.quote: Latis est connue comme la déesse de l'eau et de la bière. Elle a peut-être été associée aux rivières voisines.

claims.statement: The town of Latiscum near Vix in northern Burgundy (Bourgogne) may refer to these deities.
claims.statement_id: Kota Latiscum dekat Vix, Burgundy (Bourgogne) utara, mungkin merujuk dewa ini.
claims.quote: Le nom de la cité fossile de Latiscum élevée sur une butte isolée dans une boucle de la Seine près de Vix dans le nord Bourgogne

claims.statement: The Deus Latis dedication at Aballava, Burgh-by-Sands: DEO LATI LVCIVS VRSEI.
claims.statement_id: Persembahan Deus Latis di Aballava, Burgh-by-Sands: DEO LATI LVCIVS VRSEI.
claims.quote: The dedication to Deus Latis, recovered on an altar-stone at the Roman fort of Aballava, Burgh-by-Sands (also in Cumbria) reads: DEO LATI LVCIVS VRSEI

claims.statement: Peg Powler is a hag and water spirit of English folklore in the River Tees; like the Grindylow, Jenny Greenteeth and Nelly Longarms she drags children in.
claims.statement_id: Peg Powler nenek sihir dan roh air cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore) di Sungai Tees (River Tees); seperti Grindylow, Jenny Greenteeth, Nelly Longarms; menakuti anak; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Peg Powler is a hag and water spirit in English folklore who inhabits the River Tees. Similar to the Grindylow, Jenny Greenteeth, and Nelly Longarms, she drags children into the water if they get too close to the edge. She is regarded as a bogeyman figure who is invoked by parents to frighten children into proper behaviour.

claims.statement: William Henderson: green hair and an insatiable desire for human life.
claims.statement_id: William Henderson: rambut hijau, hasrat tak terpuaskan akan nyawa manusia.
claims.quote: The 19th century folklorist William Henderson describes Peg Powler as having green hair and "an insatiable desire for human life" and she is said to lure people into the river to drown or be devoured.

claims.statement: Foam on the Tees is called Peg Powler's suds or cream.
claims.statement_id: Buih di Sungai Tees disebut Peg Powler's suds atau Peg Powler's cream.
claims.quote: The foam or froth which is often seen floating on certain parts of the Tees is called "Peg Powler's suds" or "Peg Powler's cream".

claims.statement: Nanny Powler haunts the River Skerne; Michael Denham: Peg Powler's sister or daughter.
claims.statement_id: Nanny Powler di Sungai Skerne (River Skerne); Michael Denham: saudari atau putri Peg Powler.
claims.quote: A similar creature named Nanny Powler is said to haunt the River Skerne, a tributary of the Tees. Michael Denham regards her as either the sister or daughter of Peg Powler.

claims.statement: Elliott O'Donnell (Ghosts, Helpful and Harmful, 1924): appears as a lovely green-haired young woman pretending to drown.
claims.statement_id: Elliott O'Donnell (Ghosts, Helpful and Harmful, 1924): menjelma perempuan muda cantik berambut hijau yang pura-pura tenggelam.
claims.quote: Elliott O'Donnell paints a somewhat different picture of Peg Powler in his 1924 book Ghosts, Helpful and Harmful. He describes her as a spirit who lures men and boys to their doom in the River Tees by appearing as a beautiful young woman with green hair

claims.statement: She seizes ankles, especially of naughty children; at Mickleton in Teesdale she is the High Green Ghost (Grand Fantôme Vert).
claims.statement_id: Menangkap pergelangan kaki, terutama anak nakal; di Mickleton, Teesdale, disebut High Green Ghost (Grand Fantôme Vert).
claims.quote: Elle saisit les chevilles de ceux qui errent trop près de la rivière, particulièrement les enfants méchants, et les tire sous l'eau puis les noie. Dans la région de Mickleton, dans le Teesdale, elle est désignée sous le nom du Grand Fantôme Vert (High Green Ghost).

claims.statement: Souconna is a Celtic goddess of the river Saône at Chalon-sur-Saône.
claims.statement_id: Souconna dewi Kelt (Celtic), dewa Sungai Saône di Chalon-sur-Saône; di Prancis.
claims.quote: Souconna is a Celtic goddess, the deity of the river Saône at Chalon-sur-Saône, to whom epigraphic invocation was made.

claims.statement: Souconna was the goddess of the Saône in Celtic (keltischen) myth; the river's name from the 4th century AD; older name Arar.
claims.statement_id: Souconna dewi Sungai Saône dalam mitologi Kelt (keltischen); nama sungai sejak abad ke-4 Masehi; nama lama Arar.
claims.quote: Souconna war in der keltischen Mythologie die weibliche Gottheit des Flusses Saône. Dieser Fluss trug ab dem 4. Jahrhundert n. Chr. den Namen Souconna, der ältere Name für ihn war Arar

claims.statement: 1912: an inscription at Chalon-sur-Saône (Burgund); another near Sagonne (Cher) may be a different deity.
claims.statement_id: 1912: prasasti di Chalon-sur-Saône (Burgund, Burgundy); prasasti lain dekat Sagonne (Cher) mungkin dewa lain.
claims.quote: Im Jahre 1912 wurde eine Weiheinschrift für diese Göttin in Chalon-sur-Saône (Burgund) gefunden (ILTG 314). Ein weiterer Epigraph in der Nähe von Sagonne (Département Cher, frühere römische Provinz Gallia Aquitania) trägt zwar auch diesen Namen, es dürfte sich aber wegen der großen Distanz zwischen den beiden Fundorten möglicherweise um eine andere Gottheit handeln.

claims.statement: Ammianus Marcellinus: Sauconna, perhaps from Sac’hauna/Sac’hoon (keltisch), sleeping water (schlafendes Wasser).
claims.statement_id: Ammianus Marcellinus: Sauconna, mungkin dari Sac’hauna/Sac’hoon (keltisch), air yang tidur (schlafendes Wasser).
claims.quote: Bei Ammianus Marcellinus wird der Fluss als Sauconna bezeichnet, möglicherweise in Ableitung von Sac’hauna oder Sac’hoon (keltisch: „schlafendes Wasser“), wegen seiner langsamen Flussgeschwindigkeit.

claims.statement: Souconna is shown before a boat pouring water into a cup, or seated like a naiad (naïade).
claims.statement_id: Souconna digambarkan di depan perahu menuang air ke cawan, atau duduk seperti naiad (naïade).
claims.quote: L’image de la divinité des eaux, vit Souconna représentée, devant une embarcation versant de l’eau dans une coupelle, ou assise comme la naïade buvant l’eau de sa main

claims.statement: In the 1st century placed under the protection of Augustus (Auguste).
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-1 di bawah perlindungan Augustus (Auguste).
claims.quote: Au Ie siècle, Souconna est mise sous la protection d’Auguste

claims.statement: Probably honoured for her sacred healing waters (eaux curatives sacrées) of Gaul.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin dipuja karena air penyembuh suci (eaux curatives sacrées) Galia.
claims.quote: Cette déesse a probablement été vénérée pour ses eaux curatives sacrées de la Gaule pendant des millénaires.

claims.statement: The water bull (Scottish Gaelic tarbh-uisge) is a Scottish creature like the Manx tarroo ushtey and Irish tarbh-uisce; a nocturnal loch dweller, kinder than the water horse, amphibious and shapeshifting.
claims.statement_id: Water bull (tarbh-uisge, Gaelik Skotlandia/Scottish Gaelic) makhluk mitologi Skotlandia (Scottish), mirip tarroo ushtey Manx dan tarbh-uisce Irlandia (Irish); penghuni malam loch; lebih ramah dari kuda air (Water horse); amfibi dan berubah wujud; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The water bull, also known as tarbh-uisge in Scottish Gaelic, is a mythological Scottish creature similar to the Manx tarroo ushtey and the Irish tarbh-uisce. Generally regarded as a nocturnal resident of moorland lochs, it is usually more amiable than its equine counterpart the water horse, but has similar amphibious and shapeshifting abilities.

claims.statement: Breeds with cattle; calves with small ears; killed at birth, cannot be drowned.
claims.statement_id: Kawin dengan sapi biasa; anak bertelinga kecil; dibunuh saat lahir, tak bisa ditenggelamkan.
claims.quote: The water bull is said to reproduce with standard cattle, the resulting progeny distinguishable by the small size of their ears. According to some myths, the calves of water bulls and ordinary cows ought to be killed at birth by any method other than drowning – they cannot be killed by drowning

claims.statement: Edward Dwelly: tarbh-uisge, water bull, sea bull or cow.
claims.statement_id: Edward Dwelly: tarbh-uisge banteng air, banteng laut atau sapi (Scottish Gaelic).
claims.quote: Lexicographer Edward Dwelly translates tarbh-uisge from the Scottish Gaelic as "water bull, sea bull or cow" with the addition of "fabulous" within parentheses.

claims.statement: Shapeshifts into human form; may be a malevolent black beast, less nasty than the each-uisge; can be friendly.
claims.statement_id: Berubah menjadi manusia; bisa binatang hitam jahat, tak sejahat each-uisge (Each-uisge); bisa ramah.
claims.quote: The water bull is able to shapeshift into human form, and live on land or in water. It can be a monstrous, malevolent black beast, especially when described as a tarbh-uisge, but not as nasty as the each-uisge or water horse. It can also be amiable and sometimes helpful.

claims.statement: Belief persisted in Scotland until at least the late 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan bertahan di Skotlandia (Scotland) hingga akhir abad ke-19.
claims.quote: Belief in the existence of water bulls persisted in Scotland until at least the last quarter of the 19th century.

claims.statement: In northern regions (régions septentrionales) the calves are instead thought superior.
claims.statement_id: Bila tidak dibunuh, bencana bagi kawanan (troupeau); di wilayah utara (régions septentrionales) anak sapi justru dianggap unggul.
claims.quote: Ne pas le faire pourrait entraîner un désastre pour le troupeau. Cependant, dans les régions septentrionales, ces veaux sont au contraire considérés comme

claims.statement: In Irish mythology Abcán (Abhcán) was the dwarf poet and musician of the Tuatha Dé Danann, early Celtic gods of Ireland; he had a bronze boat with a tin sail.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Abcán (Abhcán) penyair dan musisi kerdil Tuatha Dé Danann, dewa Kelt (Celtic) Irlandia (Ireland); perahu perunggu berlayar timah; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: In Irish mythology, Abcán (modern spelling: Abhcán) was the dwarf poet and musician of the Tuatha Dé Danann, the early Celtic divinities of Ireland. He was said to have a bronze boat with a tin sail.

claims.statement: Abcán ferries Ruad from the Otherworld to seduce Aed Srónmár.
claims.statement_id: Abcán menyeberangkan Ruad dari Dunia Lain (Otherworld) untuk merayu Aed Srónmár.
claims.quote: In the story of the death of the goddess Ruad, Abcán is the dwarf that ferries her from the Otherworld to this one so that she can seduce the human, Aed Srónmár.

claims.statement: Captured by Cúchulainn, he escapes with lullabies; perhaps Fer Í.
claims.statement_id: Ditangkap Cúchulainn, bebas dengan nina bobo; mungkin Fer Í.
claims.quote: In another story, Abcán is captured by the hero, Cúchulainn. He frees himself by playing lullabies so irresistible that the warrior goes to sleep. Abcán has much in common with, and may be another name for, the dwarf musician Fer Í.

claims.statement: Per the es article Abcán is a god (dios) of Irish (irlandesa) myth, first appearing in the myth of Ruad.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, Abcán dewa (dios) mitologi Irlandia (irlandesa), pertama muncul dalam mitos Ruad.
claims.quote: Abcán (ortografía moderna: Abhcán) es un dios de la mitología irlandesa que aparece por primera vez en el mito de Ruad.

claims.statement: Mermaid song or fairy-mound music makes Ruad leap in and drown.
claims.statement_id: Nyanyian putri duyung atau musik gundukan peri membuat Ruad tenggelam.
claims.quote: The sounds of mermaids singing, or in some versions, music from a fairy mound cause her to leap into the water and drown.

claims.statement: A dwarf poet and musician (poeta y músico enano) serving the Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.statement_id: Penyair dan musisi kerdil (poeta y músico enano) yang melayani Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.quote: Se le describe como un poeta y músico enano al servicio de los Tuatha Dé Danann, las primeras deidades celtas de Irlanda.

claims.statement: The Adar Llwch Gwin are legendary Welsh birds, very large and intelligent, related to the griffin.
claims.statement_id: Adar Llwch Gwin makhluk legenda tradisi Wales (Welsh), burung besar cerdas, kerabat griffin (Griffin); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature from Welsh tradition depicted as very large and intelligent birds, often considered to be related to the griffin.

claims.statement: Given to Drudwas ap Tryffin by his fairy wife.
claims.statement_id: Diberikan kepada Drudwas ap Tryffin oleh istri perinya.
claims.quote: The Adar Llwch Gwin were given to a warrior named Drudwas ap Tryffin by his fairy wife.

claims.statement: The name is from Welsh adar bird, llwch dust, gwin wine; they understood human speech.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari kata Wales (Welsh) adar burung, llwch debu, gwin anggur; paham bahasa manusia.
claims.quote: The name derives from the Welsh words adar ("bird"), llwch ("dust"), and gwin ("wine"). These birds were said to understand human speech and to obey whatever command was given to them by their master.

claims.statement: Drudwas ordered them to kill the first man in battle; Arthur was late and the birds tore Drudwas apart.
claims.statement_id: Drudwas menyuruh membunuh orang pertama di medan perang; Arthur (King Arthur) terlambat, burung mencabik Drudwas.
claims.quote: However, when Drudwas was about to do battle with the hero Arthur he commanded them to kill the first man to enter the battle. Arthur himself was delayed and the birds ultimately turned on Drudwas when he walked onto the battlefield first, tearing him to pieces..

claims.statement: In medieval Welsh poetry the phrase meant raptors and brave men.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi Wales abad pertengahan, frasa ini untuk burung pemangsa dan orang pemberani.
claims.quote: Later, in medieval Welsh poetry, the phrase Adar Llwch Gwin came to describe all types of raptors including hawks, falcons, and brave men.

claims.statement: The birds sang a lament for their master; lyrics attributed to Llywarch Hen.
claims.statement_id: Burung-burung menyanyikan lagu ratapan untuk tuannya.
claims.quote: A legend states that the song was sung or composed by the birds to mourn the death of their master.

claims.statement: Per the br article the Adar Llwch Gwin are spirit birds (evned speredek) often likened to the griffin (gripi) in British (Preden) myth.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel br, Adar Llwch Gwin burung roh (evned speredek) sering dibandingkan dengan griffin (gripi) dalam mitologi Britania (Preden).
claims.quote: Adar Llwch Gwin zo evned speredek ha ledan keñveriet alies ouzh ar gripi e gwengelouriezh Preden,

claims.statement: The lyrics are attributed to Llywarch Hen.
claims.statement_id: Lirik dikaitkan dengan Llywarch Hen.
claims.quote: The lyrics are atributed to Llywarch Hen.

claims.statement: In Scottish folklore the beithir is a large snakelike creature or dragon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore) beithir makhluk besar mirip ular atau naga; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, the beithir is a large snakelike creature or dragon.

claims.statement: Scottish Gaelic beithir: serpent, lightning, thunderbolt; beithir-nimh, nathair; per James MacKillop wild beast, from Norse bear.
claims.statement_id: Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic) beithir: ular, kilat, petir; beithir-nimh, nathair; menurut James MacKillop binatang buas, dari Norse (Norse) beruang.
claims.quote: The Scottish Gaelic word beithir has been defined variously as "serpent", "lightning", and "thunderbolt". It is also referred to as beithir-nimh ("venomous serpent") and nathair ("serpent" and "adder"). The word may also mean "wild beast" and may be derived from the Norse for "bear" according to Celtic mythology scholar James MacKillop.

claims.statement: The largest and deadliest serpent, a dragon without wings or fire; lives in mountain caves and corries; venomous sting.
claims.statement_id: Ular terbesar dan paling mematikan, naga tanpa sayap atau napas api; di gua gunung dan corrie; sengat beracun.
claims.quote: The beithir is described as "the largest and most deadly kind of serpent", or as a dragon (but without certain typical European folklore draconic features such as wings or fiery breath). It dwells in mountainous caves and corries (valleys) and is equipped with a venomous sting.

claims.statement: The stung must reach water before the beithir; it is one of the fuath.
claims.statement_id: Yang tersengat harus ke air lebih dulu dari beithir; salah satu fuath (Fuath).
claims.quote: If a person is stung by the beithir then they must head for the nearest body of water such as a river or loch. If they can reach it before the beithir does then they are cured, but if the monster reaches it first then the victim is doomed. Another cure for the sting is water in which the head of another snake has been placed. The beithir is considered one of the fuath

claims.statement: A killed snake's head must be kept apart and destroyed, or it revives as a beithir.
claims.statement_id: Kepala ular harus dipisah jauh dan dihancurkan, atau ia hidup kembali sebagai beithir.
claims.quote: It is said that if a normal snake is killed then the head must be separated a proper distance from its body and destroyed. Otherwise, both parts will come together and the snake will return to life as a beithir.

claims.statement: A mountain (Berg) south of Glencoe, Ben Vair or Ben Vehir, recalls a beithir.
claims.statement_id: Gunung (Berg) di selatan Glencoe, Ben Vair atau Ben Vehir, mengenang beithir.
claims.quote: Ein Berg südlich von Glencoe heißt „Ben Vair“ oder „Ben Vehir“ und soll an einen Beithir erinnern, der dort Zuflucht suchte.

claims.statement: Donald Alexander Mackenzie (1935) linked the beithir with the Cailleach Bheur.
claims.statement_id: Donald Alexander Mackenzie (1935) mengaitkan beithir dengan Cailleach Bheur (Cailleach).
claims.quote: Donald Alexander Mackenzie in Scottish Folklore and Folk Life (1935) drew a possible connection between the beithir and the mythological hag known as the Cailleach Bheur.

claims.statement: Biróg (Biroge of the Mountain, Birog) in Irish folklore is the leanan sídhe or familiar of Cian, helping him woo Balor's daughter Eithne; a druidess in Lady Gregory and T. W. Rolleston.
claims.statement_id: Biróg (Biroge of the Mountain, Birog) dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore) leanan sídhe (Leanan sídhe) atau roh pendamping Cian, membantu meminang Eithne putri Balor; druid dalam Lady Gregory dan T. W. Rolleston; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: Biróg (Biroge of the Mountain, Birog), in Irish folklore is the leanan sídhe or the female familiar spirit of Cian who aids him in the folktale about his wooing of Balor's daughter Eithne. She is reinvented as a druidess in Lady Gregory and T. W. Rolleston's retellings.

claims.statement: John O'Donovan (1835): the Fomorian Balor locks Eithne in Tory Island's tower; Biroge of the Mountain helps Mac Cinnfhaelaidh.
claims.statement_id: John O'Donovan (1835): Balor (Fomorian) mengurung Eithne di menara Pulau Tory (Tory Island); Biroge of the Mountain membantu Mac Cinnfhaelaidh.
claims.quote: A version of the folktale recorded by John O'Donovan in 1835 relates how the Fomorian warrior Balor, to frustrate a prophecy that he would be killed by his own grandson, imprisons his only daughter Eithne in the tower of Tory Island, away from any contact with men. But Biroge of the Mountain helps a man called Mac Cinnfhaelaidh (Mac Kineely)

claims.statement: The messenger drowns two babies; one falls in the harbour, saved by Biróg and fostered by Gavida the smith.
claims.statement_id: Utusan menenggelamkan dua bayi; satu jatuh di pelabuhan, diselamatkan Biróg, diasuh Gavida si pandai besi.
claims.quote: The messenger drowns two of the babies, but unwittingly drops one in the harbour, where he is rescued by Biróg. She takes the child back to his father, who gives him to his brother, Gavida the smith, in fosterage.

claims.statement: Birog (Biróg) is a figure of Irish (Irlands) Celtic myth, a druidess (Druidin) or Síde.
claims.statement_id: Birog (Biróg) tokoh mitologi Kelt Irlandia (Irlands), druid perempuan (Druidin) atau Síde.
claims.quote: Birog, auch Biróg, ist der Name einer Sagengestalt aus der keltischen Mythologie Irlands, die in volkstümlichen Erzählungen genannt wird. Birog ist eine Druidin oder Síde.

claims.statement: Lebor Gabála Érenn and Cath Maige Tuired: she saves Cian's son (Lugh) from the drowning Balor intended.
claims.statement_id: Lebor Gabála Érenn dan Cath Maige Tuired: ia menyelamatkan putra Cian (Lugh) dari tenggelam yang dikehendaki Balor.
claims.quote: Im Lebor Gabála Érenn („Das Buch der Landnahmen Irlands“) und in Cath Maige Tuired („Die [zweite] Schlacht von Mag Tuired“) wird berichtet, dass sie den Sohn Cians vor dem Ertrinkungstod rettet, dem ihn sein Großvater Balor überantworten will.

claims.statement: The boy who later kills Balor is named Lugh by Lady Gregory and T. W. Rolleston.
claims.statement_id: Anak yang kelak membunuh Balor disebut Lugh oleh Lady Gregory dan T. W. Rolleston.
claims.quote: The boy (identified in the tale only as the "heir of Mac Kineely") who grows up to kill Balor, is more explicitly identified as Lugh in Lady Gregory and T. W. Rolleston' retelling.

claims.statement: Eithne bears triplets; Balor sends a messenger to drown them in a whirlpool.
claims.statement_id: Eithne melahirkan kembar tiga; Balor menyuruh menenggelamkannya di pusaran air.
claims.quote: Eithne gives birth to triplets, but Balor gathers them up in a sheet and sends a messenger to drown them in a whirlpool.

claims.statement: Cormoran is a giant of St. Michael's Mount in Cornish folklore; he built the island with his wife Cormelian and raided cattle; in the English tale Jack the Giant Killer he is Jack's first victim.
claims.statement_id: Cormoran raksasa St. Michael's Mount cerita rakyat Cornwall; pencipta pulau, istri Cormelian; merampok ternak; dalam dongeng Inggris (English) Jack the Giant Killer dibunuh Jack; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a giant associated with St. Michael's Mount in the folklore of Cornwall. Local tradition credits him with creating the island, in some versions with the aid of his wife Cormelian, and using it as a base to raid cattle from the mainland communities. Cormoran appears in the English fairy tale "Jack the Giant Killer" as the first giant slain by the hero, Jack

claims.statement: The name Cormoran first appears in Jack the Giant Killer chapbooks (Newcastle-upon-Tyne, Nottingham), not Cornish.
claims.statement_id: Nama Cormoran pertama muncul di chapbook Jack the Giant Killer (Newcastle-upon-Tyne, Nottingham), bukan asal Cornwall (Cornish).
claims.quote: The name "Cormoran" is not found in the early traditions; it first appears in the chapbook versions of the "Jack the Giant Killer" story printed in Newcastle-upon-Tyne and Nottingham, and is not of Cornish origin.

claims.statement: The name may relate to Corineus, who defeated Gogmagog.
claims.statement_id: Nama mungkin terkait Corineus yang mengalahkan Gogmagog.
claims.quote: The name may be related to Corineus, the legendary namesake of Cornwall. Corineus is associated with St. Michael's Mount, and is credited with defeating a giant named Gogmagog

claims.statement: He carried white granite at low tide to build the island.
claims.statement_id: Membawa granit putih dari daratan saat surut untuk membangun pulau.
claims.quote: According to the folklore, he carried white granite from the mainland at low tide to build the island.

claims.statement: He raided cattle; six digits on each hand and foot.
claims.statement_id: Merampok ternak; berjari enam di tiap tangan dan kaki.
claims.quote: From his post at St. Michael's Mount, Cormoran raided the countryside for cattle. He was distinguished by having six digits on each hand and foot.

claims.statement: Joseph Jacobs (English Fairy Tales): Cormoran, eighteen feet tall, three yards round, terror of the villages.
claims.statement_id: Joseph Jacobs (English Fairy Tales, Gutenberg): Cormoran raksasa delapan belas kaki, pinggang tiga yard, teror desa; Mount of Cornwall.
claims.quote: In those days the Mount of Cornwall was kept by a huge giant named Cormoran. He was eighteen feet in height, and about three yards round the waist, of a fierce and grim countenance, the terror of all the neighbouring towns and villages.
