claims.statement: He carried half a dozen oxen on his back at a time.
claims.statement_id: Memanggul setengah lusin lembu sekaligus; tinggal di gua di tengah Mount.
claims.quote: he seized on their cattle, making nothing of carrying half-a-dozen oxen on his back at a time
claims.detail: tidak bisa dibuka (fetch failed); dicek lewat arsip Wayback

claims.statement: Cormoran kicked Cormelian; the stones from her apron formed Chapel Rock.
claims.statement_id: Cormoran menendang Cormelian; batu dari celemeknya membentuk Chapel Rock.
claims.quote: When she was halfway back, Cormoran awoke to discover Cormelian bringing different stones than he wanted, and kicked her. The stones fell from her apron and formed Chapel Rock.

claims.statement: He lived in a cave in the Mount and waded to the mainland for food.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di gua di tengah Mount, menyeberang ke daratan mencari makanan.
claims.quote: He lived in a cave in the midst of the Mount, and whenever he wanted food he would wade over to the main-land
claims.detail: tidak bisa dibuka (fetch failed); dicek lewat arsip Wayback

claims.statement: Dahut (Dahud) is a princess of Breton legend, linked to the drowned city of Ys.
claims.statement_id: Dahut (Dahud) putri legenda Breton, kota tenggelam Ys; di Prancis.
claims.quote: Dahut, also spelled Dahud, is a princess in Breton legend and literature, associated with the legend of the drowned city of Ys.

claims.statement: From Old Breton da, good, and hud, magic.
claims.statement_id: Dari Breton Kuno (Old Breton) da baik dan hud sihir.
claims.quote: From Old Breton da, "good" (cf. Welsh da, same meaning), and hud, "magic" (cf. Welsh hud, same meaning).

claims.statement: 15th-century mentions lack Dahut; she first appears in Albert Le Grand's Vie des Saincts de la Bretagne Armorique (1680).
claims.statement_id: Abad ke-15 tanpa Dahut; pertama disebut Albert Le Grand, Vie des Saincts de la Bretagne Armorique (1680); Gradlon.
claims.quote: Dating to the 15th century, the earliest mentions of Ys and its king, Gradlon, do not mention Gradlon's daughter Dahut, and the king himself is to blame for the destruction of the city. Dahut was first mentioned in the third edition of Albert Le Grand's Vie des Saincts de la Bretagne Armorique (1680).

claims.statement: Ys is guarded by a dike, King Gradlon holds the keys; Dahut is wicked and lustful; the Devil seduces her.
claims.statement_id: Ys dilindungi tanggul, kunci dipegang Raja (King) Gradlon; Dahut jahat dan bernafsu; Iblis (Devil) merayunya.
claims.quote: In most retellings, the city of Ys is protected from floods by a dike, with King Gradlon possessing the keys to its gate. His daughter, Dahut, is a wicked and lustful young woman. In some versions she has many lovers, whom she murders, until the Devil himself comes to seduce her.

claims.statement: Dahut becomes a Mari-morgan or mermaid.
claims.statement_id: Dahut menjadi Mari-morgan (Morgen) atau putri duyung.
claims.quote: In some versions, Dahut transforms into a Mari-morgan or mermaid who haunts the area and can still be heard singing.

claims.statement: Dahut (Dahud) is sometimes confused with Ahès; she derives from an Otherworld (Autre Monde) woman of Celtic (celtique) myth.
claims.statement_id: Dahut (Dahud) kadang dikacaukan dengan Ahès; dari sosok perempuan Dunia Lain (Autre Monde) mitologi Kelt (celtique); breton.
claims.quote: Dahut ou Dahud, parfois confondue avec Ahès, est un personnage majeur de la légende de la ville d'Ys, l'un des récits les plus connus du légendaire breton. Issue d'une figure féminine de l'Autre Monde propre à la mythologie celtique

claims.statement: Gradlon flees on horseback; Dahut falls into the water and Gradlon escapes.
claims.statement_id: Gradlon kabur berkuda; Dahut jatuh ke air dan Gradlon selamat.
claims.quote: Gradlon attempts to flee on his horse with Dahut riding behind him, but the water almost overtakes him. He either throws Dahut off or she falls off. As soon as Dahut falls into the water, Gradlon is able to escape to safety.

claims.statement: Dahut steals the silver or gold keys and opens the gate; the sea floods the city.
claims.statement_id: Dahut mencuri kunci perak atau emas dan membuka gerbang; laut membanjiri kota.
claims.quote: Dahut steals the silver or gold keys, and during her carousing with her lover winds up opening the gate. The sea floods the city.

claims.statement: The gancanagh (Irish gean cánach, love talker) is a male fairy of Irish myth who seduces women.
claims.statement_id: Gancanagh (Irlandia/Irish gean cánach, pembicara cinta) peri lelaki mitologi Irlandia (Ireland), perayu perempuan; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: (from Irish gean cánach 'love talker') is a male fairy from the mythology of Ireland, known for seducing women.

claims.statement: Spellings geancánach, ganconer; per the Irish Folklore Commission (County Meath) also a small child.
claims.statement_id: Ejaan geancánach, ganconer; Irish Folklore Commission (County Meath): anak kecil.
claims.quote: The name has been rendered under various spellings including geancánach or ganconer. Sources collected from County Meath by the Irish Folklore Commission indicate that the word (pronounced gankanah or gankaneh) could also mean a small or precocious child

claims.statement: 1888: W. B. Yeats noted it was absent from dictionaries and little known in Connacht.
claims.statement_id: 1888: W. B. Yeats mencatat tak ada di kamus, kurang dikenal di Connacht.
claims.quote: In 1888, W. B. Yeats noted that the gancanagh was not found in dictionaries and the fairy was not well-known in Connacht.

claims.statement: The Dublin and London Magazine (1825): ganconer, fairies of the North of Ireland, little cave-dwelling men led by Captain Dearg.
claims.statement_id: The Dublin and London Magazine (1825): ganconer sebutan peri di Irlandia Utara (North of Ireland), lelaki kecil di gua, Captain Dearg.
claims.quote: In a story collected in The Dublin and London Magazine in 1825, ganconer is defined as "a name given to the fairies, alias the 'good people,' in the North of Ireland." They are described as little men who live in caves, led by Captain Dearg (The Red Captain).

claims.statement: Nicholas O’Kearney (1855): like the Leprechaun but lazier, with a dudeen pipe.
claims.statement_id: Nicholas O’Kearney (1855): mirip Leprechaun tapi lebih malas, dengan pipa dudeen.
claims.quote: According to Nicholas O’Kearney writing in 1855, the Geancanach was a little man similar to the Leprechaun, but lazier. He appeared in lonesome valleys with a dudeen, a short clay pipe which was consequently known as “the Geancanagh’s pipe.”

claims.statement: Ethna Carbery: the Love-Talker, a handsome incubus-like black-eyed fairy with no shadow; maidens waste away; banished by the cross.
claims.statement_id: Ethna Carbery: Love-Talker tampan mirip incubus, bermata hitam, tanpa bayangan; gadis layu dan mati; diusir tanda salib.
claims.quote: Irish poet Ethna Carbery characterized the “Love-Talker” as a handsome incubus-like fairy with black eyes. He has no shadow, and his approach is accompanied by a mist. He seduces maidens, leaving them to waste away and die afterwards. He is banished by the sign of the cross

claims.statement: Per the es article the gancanagh is a male spirit (espíritu masculino) of Northern Irish (Irlanda del Norte) myth who seduces women.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, gancanagh roh lelaki (espíritu masculino) mitologi Irlandia Utara (Irlanda del Norte), perayu perempuan.
claims.quote: Un gancanagh, geancanagh o ganconer (del irlandés: gean cánach, 'el que dice palabras de amor') es un espíritu fantástico masculino de la mitología de Irlanda del Norte, especialmente conocido por seducir a las mujeres.

claims.statement: A man who wasted money chasing women was said to have met a Geancanagh.
claims.statement_id: Lelaki yang menghabiskan uang mengejar perempuan disebut telah bertemu Geancanagh.
claims.quote: any man who had wasted his money chasing after women was said to have met a Geancanagh.

claims.statement: He seduced shepherdesses and milkmaids; meeting him was very unlucky.
claims.statement_id: Merayu gembala perempuan dan pemerah susu; bertemu dengannya sangat sial.
claims.quote: The Geancanagh seduced shepherdesses and milkmaids. It was considered highly unlucky to meet him

claims.statement: Yan-gant-y-tan is a demon from Brittany, France; in the Dictionnaire Infernal (1863).
claims.statement_id: Yan-gant-y-tan iblis dari Brittany, Prancis (France); dalam Dictionnaire Infernal (1863).
claims.quote: Yan-gant-y-tan in the Dictionnaire Infernal, 1863. Yan-gant-y-tan is the name of a demon from Brittany, France.

claims.statement: Collin de Plancy: Wanderer in the Night; from Breton John with the Fire, like Will o' the Wisp; an evil omen.
claims.statement_id: Collin de Plancy: Wanderer in the Night (Pengembara Malam); dari Breton: John with the Fire, seperti Will o' the Wisp (Will-o'-the-wisp); pertanda buruk.
claims.quote: Collin de Plancy, in the Dictionnaire Infernal, gives the meaning of his name as 'Wanderer in the Night', but the translation of his name from Breton seems to be cognate to 'John with the Fire' (compare Will o' the Wisp). Meeting him is said to be an evil omen.

claims.statement: He roams Finistère at night with five candles on his right hand, spun like a flaming wheel.
claims.statement_id: Berkeliaran malam di Finistère dengan lima lilin di jari tangan kanan, seperti roda api.
claims.quote: Yan-gant-y-tan wanders the nights in Finistère. He holds five candles on the five fingers of his right hand (compare Hand of Glory) and spins them about like a flaming wheel, as a result of which he is unable to turn quickly for fear of extinguishing their light.

claims.statement: A tall thin creature (grande et maigre) with a hideous face, or a hairy wild man (homme sauvage velu).
claims.statement_id: Makhluk tinggi kurus (grande et maigre) berwajah mengerikan atau lelaki liar berbulu (homme sauvage velu).
claims.quote: Le Yan-gant-y-tan est souvent représenté comme une créature grande et maigre au visage hideux et grotesque, ou bien à un homme sauvage velu.

claims.statement: Collin de Plancy: jan gant, Vagabond de la Nuit.
claims.statement_id: Collin de Plancy: jan gant, Vagabond de la Nuit; nama lain Jan-gant-i-tan.
claims.quote: Dans le Dictionnaire Infernal, l’occultiste et essayiste Collin de Plancy donne pour signification de son nom jan gant, « Vagabond de la Nuit »

claims.statement: A bag of gold on a post wards off his bad omen.
claims.statement_id: Kantong emas di tiang menangkal pertanda buruknya.
claims.quote: A sure way to ward off the bad omen of Yan-gant-y-tan is to leave a small bag of gold or of gold chain around a travelers post which Yan-gant-y-tan will steal and leave the house for another day.

claims.statement: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for Water Leaper) is an evil creature of Welsh folklore of swamps and ponds.
claims.statement_id: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Wales/Welsh: Water Leaper, Pelompat Air) makhluk jahat cerita rakyat Wales, di rawa dan kolam; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for 'Water Leaper') is an evil creature from Welsh folklore that lived in swamps and ponds.

claims.statement: A giant frog with bat's wings, no legs, a lizard tail with a sting; leaps over water on its wings.
claims.statement_id: Katak raksasa bersayap kelelawar, tanpa kaki, ekor kadal bersengat; melompat di air dengan sayap.
claims.quote: It is described as a giant frog with a bat's wings and zero legs whatsoever, and a long, lizard-like tail with a stinger at the end. It jumps across the water using its wings, hence its name.

claims.statement: Blamed for snapped fishing lines and eaten livestock and fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Disalahkan atas putusnya tali pancing, dimakannya ternak dan nelayan.
claims.quote: It was blamed for problems ranging from snapping fishing lines to eating livestock or even fishermen.

claims.statement: A giant frog (grenouille géante) with bat (chauve-souris) wings for forelegs, no hind legs, a stinging lizard (lézard) tail.
claims.statement_id: Katak raksasa (grenouille géante), sayap kelelawar (chauve-souris) menggantikan kaki depan, tanpa kaki belakang, ekor kadal (lézard) bersengat.
claims.quote: Il est décrit comme une grenouille géante avec des ailes de chauve-souris à la place des pattes avant, sans pattes arrière et avec une longue queue de lézard avec un dard à la fin.

claims.statement: Per the es article the Saltador de agua (Llamhigyn Y Dwr) is a creature of Welsh (Gales) folklore of swamps and ponds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, Saltador de agua (Llamhigyn Y Dwr) makhluk folklore Wales (Gales) di rawa dan kolam.
claims.quote: El Saltador de agua, también conocido como Llamhigyn Y Dwr, es una criatura del folclore de Gales que vivía en pantanos y charcas.

claims.statement: It breaks fishing lines, eats livestock and sometimes fishermen (pêcheurs).
claims.statement_id: Memutuskan tali pancing, memakan ternak dan kadang nelayan (pêcheurs).
claims.quote: Il provoque la rupture des lignes de pêche, mange du bétail et parfois des pêcheurs.

claims.statement: Melion is an anonymous Breton lai about a knight who becomes a werewolf for love of his treacherous wife.
claims.statement_id: Melion lai Breton anonim tentang ksatria yang menjadi serigala jadian demi cinta istrinya yang mengkhianatinya.
claims.quote: Melion is an anonymous Breton lai that tells the story of a knight who transforms into a werewolf for the love of his wife who betrays him.

claims.statement: Composed 1190–1204; one 1268 manuscript in the Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, Paris, in Picard dialect.
claims.statement_id: Disusun 1190–1204; satu naskah 1268 di Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, Paris, dialek Picard.
claims.quote: The actual date of composition is estimated between 1190 and 1204. The lai of Melion is contained in one existing manuscript: C. Paris, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, 3516, f. 343r, col. 1 - 344r, col. 4. This manuscript dates from 1268. The text is written in the Picard dialect.

claims.statement: Melion, a knight of King Arthur, marries the daughter of the King of Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Melion ksatria Raja Arthur (King Arthur), menikahi putri Raja Irlandia (King of Ireland); di Britania dan Irlandia.
claims.quote: Melion tells the story of a knight named Melion who serves King Arthur and who vows that he will never marry a woman who has loved another man. In the age of courtly love, it is impossible for Melion to find such a woman at court. One day while out hunting, Melion meets the daughter of the King of Ireland who tells him that she has never loved a man other than him.

claims.statement: His wife touches his head with the ring's stone and he becomes a wolf; she takes the ring and flees to Ireland with the squire.
claims.statement_id: Istri menyentuh kepalanya dengan batu cincin ajaib, ia menjadi serigala; istri membawa cincin dan kabur ke Irlandia (Ireland) dengan pengawal.
claims.quote: Melion promises her the meat and asks her to help him transform into a wolf using a magical ring. The wife touches Melion's head with the stone of the ring, and he heads off into the forest after the stag. Meanwhile, the wife takes Melion's clothes and the ring, and she elopes to Ireland with the squire.

claims.statement: Melion joins ten wolves; King Arthur arrives in Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Melion bergabung dengan sepuluh serigala; Raja Arthur (King Arthur) tiba di Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: Melion bands together with ten other wolves and begins killing livestock and people. The people complain to the king, who hunts down ten of the eleven, leaving Melion alone. King Arthur arrives in Ireland, and Melion goes to him.

claims.statement: Mélion becomes a wolf (loup) through a ring (anneau); a red stone (pierre vermeille) restores him.
claims.statement_id: Mélion berubah menjadi serigala (loup) karena cincin (anneau); kembali manusia dengan batu merah (pierre vermeille).
claims.quote: Mélion est un personnage issu d'un lai du même nom, qui se transforme en loup grâce à l'enchantement d'un anneau. Il demande à sa femme de le toucher ensuite avec une pierre vermeille pour qu'il redevienne un homme.

claims.statement: The squire confesses; the daughter must bring the ring to restore Melion.
claims.statement_id: Pengawal mengaku; sang putri dipaksa membawa cincin ajaib untuk memulihkan Melion.
claims.quote: The squire confesses, and the daughter is forced to come to court with the magical ring to restore Melion.

claims.statement: The Sluagh or Sluagh na marbh were hosts of the unforgiven dead in Irish and Scottish folklore; per Lewis Spence, in the Western Isles of Scotland the souls of the dead flying, with the Hallowe'en feast also the fairies' festival.
claims.statement_id: Sluagh (Irlandia Kuno/Old Irish slúag; Inggris: host) atau Sluagh na marbh rombongan arwah tak diampuni cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish) dan Skotlandia (Scottish); Lewis Spence (British): Western Isles of Scotland, jiwa orang mati, Hallowe'en; di Britania dan Irlandia. Halloween.
claims.quote: or Sluagh na marbh ('host of the dead'), were the hosts of the unforgiven dead in Irish and Scottish folklore. In the words of British folklorist Lewis Spence, "In the Western Isles of Scotland the Sluagh, or fairy host, was regarded as composed of the souls of the dead flying through the air, and the feast of the dead at Hallowe'en was likewise the festival of the fairies."

claims.statement: In crescent form like birds they carry people between islands; generally dangerous.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk bulan sabit seperti kawanan burung; membawa orang antarpulau; umumnya berbahaya.
claims.quote: Usually taking a crescent form, similar to a flight of birds, they were said to be able to approach and pick up a person from any direction and then transport them far away through the air, from one island to another. Although they would sometimes rescue humans from dangerous rock clefts, they were generally portrayed as dangerous to mortals.

claims.statement: The Scottish Gaelic Sluagh comes from Old Irish slúag, host; Proto-Celtic *slougo-.
claims.statement_id: Nama Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic) Sluagh dari Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish) slúag, rombongan; Proto-Kelt *slougo-.
claims.quote: The Scottish Gaelic name Sluagh stems from the Old Irish slúag (≈ slóg ), meaning 'host, army; crowd, assembly'.

claims.statement: A flying whirling shadow (ombre volante) with long webbed fingers and clawed legs; a smell of rotting meat (viande pourrie).
claims.statement_id: Bayangan terbang berputar (ombre volante), jari panjang berselaput, kaki bercakar; bau daging busuk (viande pourrie).
claims.quote: Le Sluagh était décrit comme une ombre volante et tourbillonnante avec de longs doigts maigres et palmés et des jambes déformées qui se terminaient par de longues griffes. Les troupeaux de Sluagh produisaient de l'ombre et un bruit de battements d'ailes et dégageait une odeur de viande pourrie.

claims.statement: The Sluagh attacked the dying (mourants) still weak in their beds.
claims.statement_id: Sluagh menyerang orang sekarat (mourants) yang masih di ranjang dan lemah.
claims.quote: Le Sluagh s'en prenait aux mourants alors qu'ils étaient encore dans leur lit et faibles.

claims.statement: At first the Sluagh could take any form; later it took human appearance (apparence humaine).
claims.statement_id: Mula-mula Sluagh dapat berwujud apa pun, lalu berwujud manusia (apparence humaine).
claims.quote: Au début, le Sluagh pouvait prendre n'importe quelle forme. Il a pris une apparence humaine dans un deuxième temps.

claims.statement: The sooterkin is a fabled mole-like creature born of women; 18th century; blamed on Dutch women and stoves.
claims.statement_id: Sooterkin makhluk kecil mirip tikus mondok yang dilahirkan perempuan; abad ke-18; dikaitkan perempuan Belanda (Dutch) dan tungku; di Belanda dan Britania.
claims.quote: A sooterkin is a fabled small mole-like creature that certain women were believed to have been capable of giving birth to. The origin of this initially jocular fantasy lies in the 18th century, and some eminent physicians of the day considered it factual. It is attributed to a tendency of Dutch women to frequently sit on stoves or use them under their petticoats to keep warm

claims.statement: John Maubray, The Female Physician: women could bear sooterkins; maternal impression.
claims.statement_id: John Maubray Inggris (English), The Female Physician: perempuan bisa melahirkan sooterkin; maternal impression.
claims.quote: The English physician John Maubray published a work entitled The Female Physician, in which he proposed that it was possible for women to give birth to sooterkins. Maubray was an advocate for maternal impression

claims.statement: The Mary Toft case (rabbits) exposed as a hoax; Dr Giovanni: The Sooterkin Dissected.
claims.statement_id: Kasus Mary Toft (kelinci) terbongkar tipuan; Dr Giovanni: The Sooterkin Dissected.
claims.quote: He was involved in the case of Mary Toft, who appeared to vindicate his theory by giving birth to rabbits, although the whole affair was eventually exposed for the hoax that it was. A person under the alias Dr Giovanni then published a paper addressed to Maubray titled The Sooterkin Dissected

claims.statement: Spelled sootikin in the Dictionary of Disgusting Facts.
claims.statement_id: Ejaan sootikin dalam Dictionary of Disgusting Facts.
claims.quote: The Dictionary of Disgusting Facts uses the variant spelling “sootikin”.

claims.statement: The Sooterkin (Suyger) is a mouse-sized (Maus) legendary creature that before the Enlightenment (Aufklärung) women were thought to bear.
claims.statement_id: Sooterkin (Suyger) makhluk kecil sebesar tikus (Maus), dipercaya sebelum Pencerahan (Aufklärung) dilahirkan perempuan.
claims.quote: Sooterkin, auch Suyger, ist eine sagenumwobene kleine Kreatur von der Größe einer Maus, von der manche Menschen in der Zeit vor der Aufklärung glaubten, dass Frauen sie unter bestimmten Umständen als Missgeburten gebären könnten.

claims.statement: John Cleveland (1654): Holland Women deliver a Sooterkin, not unlike a Rat.
claims.statement_id: John Cleveland (1654): perempuan Belanda (Holland Women) melahirkan Sooterkin mirip tikus (Rat).
claims.quote: John Cleveland hatte 1654 geschrieben: “There goes a report of the Holland Women, that together with their Children, they are delivered of a Sooterkin, not unlike to a Rat...”

claims.statement: From Dutch (holländische) farm women's habit of putting foot-warmers under their skirts.
claims.statement_id: Legenda dari kebiasaan perempuan tani Belanda (holländische) memakai penghangat kaki di bawah rok.
claims.quote: Die Legende entwickelte sich vor dem 17. Jahrhundert auf der Tatsache, dass holländische Bauersfrauen im Winter gerne Fußwärmer unter ihre Röcke stellten

claims.statement: The tangie (tongie) is a shape-shifting sea spirit of Orkney and Shetland folklore in Scotland; a sea horse or merman, as a horse or old man; covered in Fucus seaweed.
claims.statement_id: Tangie (tongie) roh laut pengubah wujud cerita rakyat Kepulauan Orkney dan Shetland, Skotlandia (Scotland); kuda laut atau duyung lelaki (Kelpie); kuda atau lelaki tua; rumput laut Fucus; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: A tangie (or tongie) is a shape-shifting sea spirit in the folklore of the Orkney and Shetland Islands in Scotland. A sea horse or merman, it takes on the appearance of either a horse or an aged man. Usually described as being covered with seaweed , its name derives from "tang" or seaweed of the genus Fucus.

claims.statement: It terrorises travellers, especially young women near lochs at night, abducting and devouring them.
claims.statement_id: Meneror pelancong, terutama perempuan muda dekat danau malam hari, diculik dan dimakan.
claims.quote: It is known for terrorizing lonely travellers, especially young women on roads at night near the lochs, whom it will abduct and devour under the water.

claims.statement: Distinct from the smaller Nuggle; can cause derangement.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari Nuggle yang lebih kecil; dapat membuat gila.
claims.quote: Similar yet distinctive from the smaller, less harmful Nuggle, a tangie is able to cause derangement in humans and animals.

claims.statement: The Shetland legend of Black Eric, a sheep rustler who rode a tangie.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Shetland Black Eric, pencuri domba yang menunggangi tangie.
claims.quote: The tangie plays a major role in the Shetland legend of Black Eric, a sheep rustler. The tangie he rode gave him supernatural assistance when he raided and harassed surrounding crofts.

claims.statement: Black Eric fell to his death against Sandy Breamer; the tangie kept terrorising the area.
claims.statement_id: Black Eric tewas jatuh ke laut melawan Sandy Breamer; tangie terus meneror.
claims.quote: In his final battle with crofter Sandy Breamer, Black Eric fell to his death in the sea. The tangie then continued to terrorize the area

claims.statement: Per the ru article the танги (Танги), like the nuggle (ноглом), can drive people or animals mad.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ru, танги (Танги) mirip nogl (ноглом), dapat membuat orang atau hewan gila.
claims.quote: Сходный с ноглом, но не идентичный ему, танги может свести человека или животное с ума.

claims.statement: In Celtic myth Adsullata was a river goddess of the Continental Celts tied to the Savus (Sava) in Noricum; later a hot-spring goddess in Brittany and origin of the Anglo-Celtic sun goddess Sul.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Kelt (Celtic mythology) Adsullata dewi sungai Kelt Daratan (Continental Celts), Sungai Savus (Sava), Noricum; ke Brittany dari Galia Kelt (Celtic Gaul); dewi air panas, asal dewi matahari Anglo-Kelt (Anglo-Celtic) Sul (Sulis).
claims.quote: In Celtic mythology, Adsullata was a river goddess of the Continental Celts associated with the River Savus (Sava) in Noricum. Later she came to Brittany from Celtic Gaul and was believed to be a goddess of hot springs and the origin of the Anglo-Celtic sun goddess, Sul.

claims.statement: From Proto-Celtic *Ad-sūg-lat-ā, sucking liquid; Romano-British *Adsuglata.
claims.statement_id: Dari Proto-Kelt (Proto-Celtic) *Ad-sūg-lat-ā, cairan isap; bentuk Romawi-Britania (Romano-British) *Adsuglata.
claims.quote: This theonym appears to be derived from Proto-Celtic *Ad-sūg-lat-ā. That derivation literally means (allative) "sucking liquid", which may have been a byword for the notion of "suck-giving liquid" The Romano-British form of this Proto-Celtic reconstruction would likely have been *Adsuglata.

claims.statement: Per the sr article, Адсулата (Adsullata) was a river goddess (речна богиња) of Celtic (келтској) myth, most likely of the Sava (Саве).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel sr, Адсулата (Adsullata) dewi sungai (речна богиња) mitologi Kelt (келтској), kemungkinan dewi Sava (Саве).
claims.quote: Адсулата (лат. Adsullata) је била речна богиња у келтској митологији. Највероватније је била богиња Саве.

claims.statement: The name is from Proto-Celtic (пра-келтске) Ad-sūg-lat-ā, she who draws water.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Proto-Kelt (пра-келтске) Ad-sūg-lat-ā, dia yang menimba air.
claims.quote: Име ове богиње је изведено од пра-келтске речи Ad-sūg-lat-ā, што буквално значи она која црпи воду.

claims.statement: Per the tr article, known from one inscription at Saudörfel, Austria (Avusturya).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel tr, dikenal dari satu prasasti di Saudörfel, Austria (Avusturya).
claims.quote: Avusturya, Saudörfel'de bulunan tek bir yazıttan bilinenlere dayalı bir ilahtır.

claims.statement: An article in The Celtic Review says that in Noricum the worship of Adsalluta was closely associated with that of Savus, the river Save.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah artikel dalam The Celtic Review menyebut bahwa di Noricum pemujaan Adsalluta berkaitan erat dengan pemujaan Savus, sungai Save.
claims.quote: In Noricum we find the worship of Adsalluta closely associated with that of Savus, the river Save.

claims.statement: The article says that at Saudörfel her name occurs on five inscriptions, two of which associate it with Savus.
claims.statement_id: Artikel itu menyebut bahwa di Saudörfel namanya muncul pada lima prasasti, dua di antaranya dikaitkan dengan Savus.
claims.quote: At Saudörfel her name occurs on five inscriptions, on two of which it is associated with that of Savus.

claims.statement: The article adds that at Hrastnigg her name also occurs on an inscription reading Adsal(l)ute Aug(uste).
claims.statement_id: Artikel itu menambahkan bahwa di Hrastnigg namanya juga muncul pada sebuah prasasti yang berbunyi Adsal(l)ute Aug(uste).
claims.quote: At Hrastnigg, too, her name occurs on an inscription which reads Adsal(l)ute Aug(uste).

claims.statement: Arkan sonney (Manx), lucky urchin or plentiful little pig, is the Manx term for hedgehog.
claims.statement_id: Arkan sonney (Manx), landak keberuntungan atau babi kecil berlimpah, sebutan Manx untuk landak; di Isle of Man.
claims.quote: Arkan sonney (/ˈɑːrkən ˈsɒni/; Manx pronunciation: ['aːrkan ˈsonə] , literally "lucky urchin" or "plentiful little pig") is the Manx term for hedgehog.

claims.statement: A fairy animal shaped like a white pig bringing fortune; seeing the lucky piggy is a good omen.
claims.statement_id: Hewan peri berwujud babi putih pembawa keberuntungan; melihat lucky piggy pertanda baik.
claims.quote: The arkan sonney is a type of fairy animal that takes the form of a white pig that brings good fortune to those who manage to catch it. It was even considered a favourable omen just to have seen the "lucky piggy".

claims.statement: Catching one means a silver coin always in your pocket; holding it too long brings bad luck.
claims.statement_id: Menangkapnya: selalu ada koin perak di saku; menahan terlalu lama membawa sial.
claims.quote: It was also said that if you caught one you would always find a silver coin in your pocket. However, holding on to it for too long will result in bad fortune.

claims.statement: Fairy Tales From the Isle of Man (1951) by Dora Broome: red eyes and ears; changes size, not shape.
claims.statement_id: Fairy Tales From the Isle of Man (1951), Dora Broome: mata dan telinga merah, ubah ukuran bukan wujud.
claims.quote: In Fairy Tales From the Isle of Man (1951) by Dora Broome, the white pig is described as having red eyes and ears, and though it can alter its size it is not able to change its shape.

claims.statement: Per the no article, Manx (mansk) tales tell of a nisse- or elf-like (alv) being like a long-eared hedgehog (piggsvin); catching one brings luck.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel no, dalam cerita rakyat Manx (mansk) makhluk seperti nisse atau elf (alv), seperti landak (piggsvin) bertelinga panjang; menangkapnya membawa keberuntungan.
claims.quote: I mansk folkeminne finnes det fortellinger om en form for vesen, nisse eller alv, som ser ut som en piggsvin med lange ører. Det er sagt at de er lykkebringende å fange dem.

claims.statement: Per the fr article, in Isle of Man (île de Man) folklore an arkan sonney is a hedgehog (hérisson).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel fr, dalam folklore Isle of Man (île de Man) arkan sonney berarti landak (hérisson).
claims.quote: Dans le folklore de l'île de Man, un arkan sonney désigne un hérisson.

claims.statement: The bauchan (Scottish bòcan; English bauchan, buckawn, bogan) is a domestic hobgoblin of Scottish folklore, mischievous, sometimes dangerous, but helpful.
claims.statement_id: Bauchan (Skotlandia/Scottish bòcan; Inggris/English bauchan, buckawn, bogan) hobgoblin (Hobgoblin) rumah tangga cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore); jahil, berbahaya, membantu; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The bauchan (Scottish: bòcan English: bauchan, buckawn or bogan) is a type of domestic hobgoblin in Scottish folklore. It is often mischievous and sometimes dangerous, but is also very helpful when the need arises.

claims.statement: John Francis Campbell (Popular Tales of the West Highlands): Callum Mor MacIntosh's farm in Lochaber was haunted by a bauchan.
claims.statement_id: John Francis Campbell (Popular Tales of the West Highlands): pertanian Callum Mor MacIntosh di Lochaber dihantui bauchan.
claims.quote: John Francis Campbell in his Popular Tales of the West Highlands tells the story of Callum Mor MacIntosh whose farm in Lochaber was haunted by a bauchan. The relationship between Callum and the bauchan was noted as being contradictory in nature.

claims.statement: It followed Callum to New York City and helped clear his land; it can become a goat.
claims.statement_id: Ikut Callum ke New York City dan membantu membuka lahan; dapat menjadi kambing.
claims.quote: When Callum emigrated to New York City the bauchan went with him and helped him clear his new plot of land. In this tale the bauchan is a shapeshifter and is able to transform into a goat.

claims.statement: Per the es article the bauchan (bòcan, bogan, buckawn) is a Celtic (celta) creature, a type of brownie, male or female, hairy, mischievous, solitary.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, bauchan (bòcan, bogan, buckawn) makhluk mitologi Kelt (celta), sejenis brownie (Brownie), lelaki atau perempuan, berbulu, jahil, penyendiri.
claims.quote: Un bauchan (también bòcan [Ir.], bogan o buckawn) es una criatura de la mitología celta, un tipo de brownie. Podían ser tanto masculino como femenino. Se caracterizarían por tener mucho pelo, ser traviesos y solitarios.

claims.statement: The bauchan was belligerent yet helped with farm tasks.
claims.statement_id: Bauchan suka berkelahi tetapi membantu pekerjaan pertanian.
claims.quote: While the bauchan was belligerent and combative, he often provided assistance in various farm-related tasks.

claims.statement: The compiler's note in the collection says that the supernatural being called Bauchan is probably Bocan, a little buck, a hobgoblin, a ghost.
claims.statement_id: Catatan penyusun kumpulan itu menyatakan bahwa makhluk gaib yang disebut Bauchan itu mungkin Bocan, yakni seekor jantan kecil, hantu rumah (hobgoblin), atau hantu.
claims.quote: as Bauchan, is probably Bocan, a little buck, a hobgoblin, a ghost

claims.statement: According to the compiler's note, in the next tale the same being appears fully tamed: still supernatural and possessed of extraordinary strength, but attached to a family, and a regular brownie.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan penyusun kumpulan itu, dalam kisah berikutnya makhluk itu tampil sepenuhnya jinak: tetap gaib dan berkekuatan luar biasa, tetapi melekat pada sebuah keluarga, dan seorang brownie yang sesungguhnya.
claims.quote: the same being appears fully tamed ; still supernatural, still possessed of extraordinary strength, but attached to a family, and a regular brownie.

claims.statement: In the tale recorded in the collection, a farmer near Loch Traig in Lochaber held a small farm and there were rumours that he had dealings with a mysterious personage called a bauchan, with no authentic account of how they first met.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat dalam kumpulan itu, di sekitar Loch Traig di Lochaber seorang petani memiliki pertanian kecil dan beredar desas-desus bahwa ia bergaul dengan sosok misterius bernama bauchan, tanpa catatan otentik tentang perkenalan pertama mereka.
claims.quote: In the neighbourhood of Loch Traig, in Lochaber, ... held a little farm. There were rumours of his having intercourse with a mysterious personage called a bauchan, but of his first acquaintance with him there are no authentic accounts.

claims.statement: According to the tale, on some occasions the farmer was supernaturally aided by the bauchan, while at others, having somehow roused its displeasure, he was opposed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah itu, pada beberapa kesempatan sang petani dibantu secara gaib oleh bauchan itu, sedangkan pada kesempatan lain, karena entah bagaimana membangkitkan kemarahannya, ia dihalangi.
claims.quote: that on some occasions he was supernaturally aided by this bauchan, while at others, having in some way excited his displeasure

claims.statement: In the tale, on several occasions the two came to fighting hand to hand.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, beberapa kali mereka sampai berkelahi tangan kosong.
claims.quote: on several occasions they came the length of fighting hand to hand

claims.statement: In the tale, when the farmer wished for the tree he had felled, the house shook and the door rattled, and there was the wished-for tree with the Bauchan grinning at him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, ketika sang petani menyatakan keinginannya akan pohon yang ia tebang, rumah berguncang dan pintu bergetar, dan di sana tergeletak pohon yang diinginkan, dengan Bauchan menyeringai kepadanya.
claims.quote: Hardly had he spoken when the house was shaken and the door rattled ... and there was the wished-for tree, with the Bauchan grinning at him

claims.statement: In the tale, Callum found his forgotten hogshead, hides and all, transported five miles across very rugged, rocky country.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, Callum menemukan tong besarnya yang tertinggal, lengkap dengan kulit di dalamnya, telah dipindahkan sejauh lima mil melalui daerah berbatu yang sangat terjal.
claims.quote: what did Callum see but his own identical hogshead, hides and all. It had been transported the distance of five miles of most rugged, rocky district.

claims.statement: In the tale, when the farmer stepped ashore in New York, who should meet him but the Bauchan in the shape of a goat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, ketika sang petani menjejak daratan di New York, yang menemuinya adalah Bauchan dalam wujud kambing.
claims.quote: who should meet him in the shape of a goat but the Bauchan

claims.statement: The tale closes with rumour that Callum benefited from the Bauchan's help in clearing the lands of his new settlement.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu menutup dengan kabar bahwa Callum diuntungkan oleh bantuan Bauchan dalam membuka tanah permukiman barunya.
claims.quote: rumour says that Callum was the better of the Bauchan's help in clearing the lands of his new settlement

claims.statement: In another tale in the collection, Coluinn gun Cheann ("the Headless Trunk") is a very celebrated Bauchkan who favoured the family of the Macdonals of Morar from time immemorial.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah lain dalam kumpulan itu, Coluinn gun Cheann ("Batang Tanpa Kepala") adalah Bauchkan yang sangat termasyhur, yang sejak zaman purba berpihak pada keluarga Macdonal dari Morar.
claims.quote: Coluinn gun Cheann was a very celebrated Bauchkan, who favoured the family of the Macdonals of Morar, for ages immemorial

claims.statement: According to the tale, Coluinn gun Cheann waged war especially with all the strong men he could meet with.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah itu, Coluinn gun Cheann berperang terutama melawan orang-orang kuat yang ia temui.
claims.quote: and waged war, especially with all the strong men he could meet with

claims.statement: According to the tale, he was seldom, if ever, seen by women and did no harm either to them or to children.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah itu, ia jarang atau tidak pernah terlihat oleh perempuan dan tidak mencelakai mereka maupun anak-anak.
claims.quote: He was seldom, if ever, seen by women, and did no harm either to them or to children.

claims.statement: According to the tale, before sunrise the Coluinn had to be off, as he never could be seen in daylight.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah itu, sebelum matahari terbit Coluinn harus pergi karena ia tidak pernah dapat terlihat di siang hari.
claims.quote: Before sunrise it was necessary for the Coluinn to be off, as he never could be seen in daylight.

claims.statement: The character "Buckeye" is a bauchan in the fantasy novel The Haunted Wizard (1999) by Christopher Stasheff.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh "Buckeye" adalah seorang bauchan dalam novel fantasi The Haunted Wizard (1999) karya Christopher Stasheff.
claims.quote: The character "Buckeye" is a bauchan in the fantasy novel The Haunted Wizard (1999) by Christopher Stasheff.

claims.statement: The Black Lady of Bradley Woods is a ghost of the woods near Bradley, Lincolnshire, England.
claims.statement_id: Black Lady of Bradley Woods hantu hutan dekat Bradley, Lincolnshire, Inggris (England); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The Black Lady of Bradley Woods is a ghost which reportedly haunts the woods near the village of Bradley, Lincolnshire, England.

claims.statement: Young and pretty, 168 cm, black cloak and hood, pale tear-soaked face; never harmed anyone.
claims.statement_id: Muda dan cantik, 168 cm, jubah dan tudung hitam, wajah pucat basah air mata; tak pernah mencelakai.
claims.quote: Alleged eyewitnesses have described her as being young and pretty, around 5 ft 6 in (168 cm) tall, dressed in a flowing black cloak and a black hood that obscures her hair but reveals her mournful, pale, tear-soaked face. According to the legend she has never harmed anyone

claims.statement: Used by parents to scare children: the black lady will get you.
claims.statement_id: Dipakai orang tua menakuti anak: the black lady will get you; turun-temurun.
claims.quote: It was once used by parents to frighten children; this appears to have been a common practice among parents in the area, and children were warned that if they were not safely in bed by a certain time, "the black lady will get you!".

claims.statement: During the Wars of the Roses or Barons' Wars a woodsman went to war.
claims.statement_id: Masa Perang Mawar (Wars of the Roses) atau Perang Para Baron (Barons' Wars), penebang kayu pergi berperang.
claims.quote: During the Wars of the Roses, or alternatively the Barons' Wars, a young woodsman and his wife lived with their baby son in a cottage in Bradley Woods. Eventually the woodsman went off to fight in the wars, leaving his wife to bring up the baby alone.

claims.statement: Attacked by three horsemen who took her baby; she searched in vain; after death she was seen in the woods.
claims.statement_id: Diserang tiga penunggang kuda, bayinya dirampas; mencari anak dan suami; setelah mati terlihat di hutan.
claims.quote: As she was leaving her cottage, the woman was set upon by three horsemen who brutally raped her before snatching the baby boy and riding off laughing into the woods. Heartbroken and humiliated, she wandered the woods searching in vain for her child and husband. After her death people began to see her wandering the woods

claims.statement: Per the sv article the story (Historien) has been told for many generations (generationer).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel sv, kisah (Historien) diceritakan selama banyak generasi (generationer).
claims.quote: Historien är känd för att ha berättats i många generationer.

claims.statement: She waited daily at the wood's edge until the enemy crossed the Humber.
claims.statement_id: Setiap hari menunggu di tepi hutan sampai pasukan musuh menyeberangi Humber.
claims.quote: Every day she held her child and walked to the edge of the woods, waiting for the sight of her husband coming home, until one day the enemy army crossed the Humber

claims.statement: Bleiddwn (Welsh blaidd, wolf) appears in the fourth of the Four Branches of the Mabinogi, a son of Gwydion and Gilfaethwy.
claims.statement_id: Bleiddwn (Wales/Welsh blaidd, serigala) dalam cabang keempat Four Branches of the Mabinogi, putra Gwydion dan Gilfaethwy; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Bleiddwn (from the Welsh blaidd, "Wolf") appears in the fourth of the Four Branches of the Mabinogi and is one of the three sons of Gwydion and Gilfaethwy.

claims.statement: Math punished them (rape of Goewin) as deer, pigs, wolves; their young Hyddwn, Hychddwn and Bleiddwn, the last from the wolves.
claims.statement_id: Math menghukum mereka (pemerkosaan Goewin) menjadi rusa, babi, serigala; anak Hyddwn, Hychddwn, Bleiddwn dari pasangan serigala.
claims.quote: As punishment for the rape of Goewin, Math banished his nephews, turning them into a breeding pair of deer for a year, then pigs, and finally wolves. They had three children over the three years: Hyddwn, Hychddwn, and Bleiddwn. Bleiddwn is the offspring of the wolf pairing.

claims.statement: Math made him human and named him Bleiddwn (Wolf-man).
claims.statement_id: Math mengubahnya menjadi manusia, membaptisnya Bleiddwn (Wolf-man).
claims.quote: Math took him and transformed him into a human being, baptising him Bleiddwn ("Wolf-man").

claims.statement: Bleiddwn (petit loup) is a fabulous wolf cub (louveteau fabuleux) of Brittonic (brittonique) myth in the Fourth Branch (Quatrième branche), Math son of Mathonwy.
claims.statement_id: Bleiddwn (petit loup) anak serigala ajaib (louveteau fabuleux) mitologi Kelt Britonik (brittonique), Cabang Keempat Mabinogi (Quatrième branche), Math fab Mathonwy.
claims.quote: Bleiddwn (« petit loup ») est un louveteau fabuleux de la mythologie celtique brittonique, qui apparaît dans la Quatrième branche du Mabinogi : « Math fils de Mathonwy ».

claims.statement: Fathered by Gwydion and Gilfaethwy as wolf and she-wolf (loup, louve) by Math's magic.
claims.statement_id: Diperanakkan Gwydion dan Gilfaethwy saat berwujud serigala (loup, louve) karena sihir Math.
claims.quote: Il est engendré par les deux frères Gwydion et Gilfaethwy, alors qu’ils ont l’apparence respective d’un loup et d’une louve, états dus à la magie de leur oncle Math.

claims.statement: Math, magician and ruler of Gwynedd (souverain du Gwynedd).
claims.statement_id: Math, penyihir dan penguasa Gwynedd (souverain du Gwynedd).
claims.quote: Math, magicien et souverain du Gwynedd, est contraint de vivre les pieds dans le giron de la vierge Goewin, à moins qu’il ne doive aller à la guerre.

claims.statement: Bloody Bones is a bogeyman of English and North American folklore, first written about 1548; also Rawhead, Tommy Rawhead, Rawhead-and-Bloody-Bones.
claims.statement_id: Bloody Bones momok (bogeyman, Bogeyman) cerita rakyat Inggris (English) dan Amerika Utara (North American), sejak sekitar 1548; juga Rawhead, Tommy Rawhead, Rawhead-and-Bloody-Bones.
claims.quote: Bloody Bones is a bogeyman figure in English and North American folklore whose first written appearance is approximately 1548. As with all bogeymen the figure has been used to frighten children into proper deportment. The character is sometimes called Rawhead, Tommy Rawhead, or Rawhead-and-Bloody-Bones (with or without the hyphens).

claims.statement: John Locke (1693): used to awe children; Samuel Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language (1755): Rawhead, a spectre to fright children.
claims.statement_id: John Locke (1693): untuk menakuti anak; Samuel Johnson, Dictionary of the English Language (1755): nama hantu (Rawhead).
claims.quote: The term "Raw-Head and Bloody-Bones, and such other Names" was used "to awe children, and keep them in subjection", as recorded by John Locke in 1693. Samuel Johnson in his Dictionary of the English Language (first published in 1755) defined "Rawhead" as "the name of a spectre, mentioned to fright children".

claims.statement: From Great Britain, especially Lancashire and Yorkshire, spreading to the Southern United States.
claims.statement_id: Berasal dari Britania Raya (Great Britain), Lancashire dan Yorkshire, menyebar ke Amerika Utara (North America), Amerika Serikat bagian selatan (Southern United States); di Britania dan AS.
claims.quote: The stories originated in Great Britain where they were particularly common in Lancashire and Yorkshire, and spread to North America where the stories were common in the Southern United States.

claims.statement: A water demon of ponds and marl pits dragging children down, like the grindylow and Jenny Greenteeth.
claims.statement_id: Iblis air di kolam dan lubang marl, menyeret anak seperti grindylow (Grindylow) dan Jenny Greenteeth.
claims.quote: Bloody Bones is sometimes regarded as a water demon haunting deep ponds, oceans, and old marl pits (which often became filled with water to form ponds) where it dragged children into the depths, much like the grindylow and Jenny Greenteeth.

claims.statement: Old Bloody Bones is a Cornish version per F. W. Jones, living in Knockers Hole near Baldhu.
claims.statement_id: Old Bloody Bones versi Cornwall (Cornish) menurut F. W. Jones, di Knockers Hole dekat Baldhu.
claims.quote: Old Bloody Bones is a Cornish version of Rawhead-and-Bloody-Bones according to F. W. Jones in Old Cornwall. Old Bloody Bones inhabited Knockers Hole near the village of Baldhu.

claims.statement: Bloody Bones is a being feared by children (Kindern), a demon (Dämon) or ghost (Geist).
claims.statement_id: Bloody Bones makhluk yang ditakuti anak (Kindern), iblis (Dämon) atau hantu (Geist).
claims.quote: Bloody Bones ist in Teilen des englischsprachigen Raumes ein von Kindern gefürchtetes Wesen, ein Dämon oder Geist.

claims.statement: Ruth Tongue (Somerset Folklore): lived in a dark cupboard under the stairs.
claims.statement_id: Ruth Tongue (Somerset Folklore): tinggal di lemari gelap di bawah tangga.
claims.quote: Ruth Tongue said in Somerset Folklore that he "lived in a dark cupboard, usually under the stairs.

claims.statement: Rewards good children, punishes naughty ones by dragging them down the drain (Abflussrohr) or into water and drowning them.
claims.statement_id: Menghadiahi anak baik, menghukum anak nakal: menyeret ke saluran air (Abflussrohr) atau air dan menenggelamkan.
claims.quote: Rawhead und Bloody Bones belohnen sehr brave Kinder, bestrafen aber unartige Kinder, indem sie sie das Abflussrohr hinunter oder ins Wasser hinein ziehen und sie ertränken.

claims.statement: The bluecap is a fairy or ghost of English folklore living in mines as a small blue flame, leading respectful miners to minerals.
claims.statement_id: Bluecap peri atau hantu cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), di tambang, nyala api biru kecil; menuntun ke mineral; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: A bluecap is a mythical fairy or ghost in English folklore that inhabits mines and appears as a small blue flame. If miners treat them with respect, the bluecaps lead them to rich deposits of minerals.

claims.statement: Like knockers or kobolds they warn of cave-ins; associated with the Anglo-Scottish borders.
claims.statement_id: Seperti knocker (Knocker) atau kobold (Kobold), memperingatkan runtuhan; perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish).
claims.quote: Like knockers or kobolds, bluecaps can also forewarn miners of cave-ins. They are mostly associated with the Anglo-Scottish borders.

claims.statement: Hard workers paid like a putter; wages left in a corner; neither more nor less.
claims.statement_id: Pekerja keras, dibayar setara putter; upah di sudut tambang; tak lebih tak kurang.
claims.quote: Bluecaps were regarded as hard workers and it was said that they were expected to be paid a working man's wages, equal to those of an average putter (a mine worker who pushes the wagons). This payment was left in a solitary corner of the mine, and they would not accept any more or less than they were owed.

claims.statement: A flickering bluecap moved a full tub of coal.
claims.statement_id: Bluecap berkelip memindahkan tong batu bara penuh.
claims.quote: The miners would sometimes talk of having seen a flickering bluecap settle on a full tub of coal, transporting it as though "impelled by the sturdiest sinews".

claims.statement: Per the zh article 藍帽子 (Bluecap) is a small fairy or ghost of English folklore in mines, a blue flame.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel zh, 藍帽子 (Bluecap) peri kecil atau hantu cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), di tambang, nyala biru.
claims.quote: 藍帽子（英語：Bluecap）是一種英國民間傳說（英语：English folklore）中虛構的小仙子或幽靈。他們居住在礦山內，並以微小的藍色火焰形象出現。

claims.statement: Cutty Soames (Old Cutty Soames) cut the putters' rope-traces.
claims.statement_id: Cutty Soames (Old Cutty Soames) memotong tali pengikat putter.
claims.quote: Another being of the same type (though less helpful in nature) was called "Cutty Soames" or Old Cutty Soames, who was known to cut the rope-traces or soams by which the assistant putter was yoked to the tub.

claims.statement: In the Book of Leinster list of rath- and castle-builders Balor is son of Buarainech; Cath Maige Tuired calls Balor son of Néit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar pembangun rath dan benteng di Book of Leinster, Balor disebut putra Buarainech; Cath Maige Tuired menyebut Balor putra Néit.
claims.quote: called Balor son of Buarainech in the list of renowned rath- and castle-builders of the world, preserved in the Book of Leinster

claims.statement: Buareinech is the son of the Irish war god Neit and one of the Fomori (Fomorians); his son Balor is their king.
claims.statement_id: Buareinech putra dewa perang Irlandia Neit, anggota kaum Fomori (Fomorians); putranya Balor, raja kaum itu.
claims.quote: Buareinech ist der Sohn des irischen Kriegsgottes Neit und ein Angehöriger des Volkes der Fomori. Sein Sohn ist Balor, der König dieses Volkes.

claims.statement: In Irish mythology (Ireland), Buarainech is a giant, father of Balar (Balor), king of the Fomorians; Squire: cow-faced.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irlanda, Ireland), Buarainech raksasa, ayah Balar (Balor), raja Fomori; Squire: berwajah sapi.
claims.quote: En la mitología irlandesa, Buarainech era un gigante, padre de Balar, el rey de los fomorianos, seres semi-divinos que habrían habitado Irlanda en tiempos inmemoriales. Squire glosa el nombre como 'con cara de vaca'.

claims.statement: In the Cath Maige Tuired, Lugh destroys Balor's eye and beheads him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Cath Maige Tuired, Lugh menghancurkan mata Balor dan memenggalnya.
claims.quote: In der Cath Maige Tuired („Die [Zweite] Schlacht von Mag Tuired“) kann Lugh dieses Auge zerstören und Balor enthaupten.

claims.statement: The child Balor peeks into the druids' cauldron of Buarainech, loses an eye and becomes a cyclops (Zyklop) with a deadly gaze.
claims.statement_id: Balor kecil mengintip kuali ramuan druid Buarainech, kehilangan satu mata, menjadi Zyklop bertatapan mematikan.
claims.quote: wirft Balor als Kind heimlich einen Blick in den Kessel, verliert ein Auge und wird dadurch zu einem Zyklopen mit tödlichem Blick

claims.statement: Squire translates the name of Buareinech as Kuh-Gesicht (cow-faced), fitting the typical Fomori look.
claims.statement_id: Squire menerjemahkan nama Buareinech sebagai Kuh-Gesicht (berwajah sapi), cocok dengan rupa khas Fomori.
claims.quote: Buareinechs Name wird von Squire mit „Kuh-Gesicht“ übersetzt. Dies passt zu dem für die Fomori als typischem, in der Mythologie tradiertem Aussehen

claims.statement: Cavall (Cafall, Cabal) was King Arthur's favourite dog, used to hunt Twrch Trwyth (Troynt); last dog loosed in a stag hunt (Gereint Son of Erbin); Welsh tradition.
claims.statement_id: Cavall (Cafall, Cabal) anjing kesayangan Raja Arthur (King Arthur), dipakai memburu Twrch Trwyth (Troynt); anjing terakhir dilepas dalam perburuan rusa (Gereint Son of Erbin); tradisi Welsh.
claims.quote: was King Arthur's dog, used in the hunt for the great boar, Twrch Trwyth (Latin: Troynt, Troit ). Cavall was Arthur's "favourite dog", and during a stag hunt, he was customarily the last dog to be let loose to chase after the game (Gereint Son of Erbin).

claims.statement: Historia Brittonum (9th century) mentions Cabal's pawprint in rock while chasing Troynt (Wonders of Britain).
claims.statement_id: Historia Brittonum (abad ke-9) menyebut jejak kaki Cabal di batu saat memburu Troynt (Wonders of Britain).
claims.quote: the mention Arthur's dog Cabal's pawprint, preserved in rock, in the Latin tract of Historia Brittonum (9th century). The print was preserved in rock while the dog was pursuing the boar Troynt.

claims.statement: Cabal left his print in the stone; Arthur heaped the mound Carn Cabal in the Buelt region of Britain.
claims.statement_id: Cabal meninggalkan jejak di batu; Arthur menumpuk gundukan Carn Cabal di wilayah Buelt, Britania (Britain).
claims.quote: When Cabal, who was the dog of Arthur the soldier, was hunting the boar Troynt (recté Troit), he impressed his print in the stone, and afterwards Arthur assembled a stone mound under the stone with the print of his dog, and it is called the Carn Cabal (i.e., a cairn).

claims.statement: A stone carried off is found back on its mound the next day.
claims.statement_id: Batu yang dibawa pergi ditemukan lagi di atas gundukannya keesokan harinya.
claims.quote: And men come and remove the stone in their hands for the length of a day and a night; and on the next day it is found on top of its mound.

claims.statement: Cabal (Caval, Cavall, Cafal) was King Arthur's dog (Kung Arturs hund), mentioned in Historia Brittonum.
claims.statement_id: Cabal (Caval, Cavall, Cafal) anjing Raja Arthur (Kung Arturs hund), disebut dalam Historia Brittonum.
claims.quote: Cabal (latinskt namn; stavas ibland Caval, Cavall eller Cafal) var Kung Arturs hund, som bland annat omnämns i Historia Brittonum.

claims.statement: The Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen names many dogs besides Cavall in the party hunting Twrch Trwyth.
claims.statement_id: Roman Welsh Culhwch and Olwen menyebut banyak anjing selain Cavall dalam rombongan pemburu Twrch Trwyth.
claims.quote: the late Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen weaves a much more intricate tale, naming many dogs besides Cavall in the hunting party

claims.statement: Similarity of the name to Latin caballus (horse); R. J. Thomas, 1936.
claims.statement_id: Kemiripan nama dengan kata Latin caballus (kuda); R. J. Thomas, 1936.
claims.quote: A number of scholars have commented upon the similarity of the dog's name to the Latin word caballus for "horse". In an article from 1936, R. J. Thomas said that

claims.statement: The name Buelt survives in Builth Wells, now in county Powys, Wales.
claims.statement_id: Nama Buelt bertahan dalam Builth Wells, kini bagian county Powys, Wales.
claims.quote: The "Buelt" name is also preserved in present-day Builth Wells (in historic county of Brecknockshire) now part of county Powys.

claims.statement: The ceasg is a mermaid of Scottish folklore with a woman's body and a grilse tail; called maighdean na tuinne / maighdean mhara in Scottish Gaelic.
claims.statement_id: Ceasg putri duyung folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Skotlandia), tubuh perempuan cantik berekor grilse; disebut maighdean na tuinne / maighdean mhara dalam Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic).
claims.quote: The ceasg [kʲʰɛsk] is a mermaid in Scottish folklore with the upper body of a beautiful woman merging with the tail of a grilse (a young salmon). She is also known in Scottish Gaelic as maighdean na tuinne ("maid of the wave") or maighdean mhara ("maid of the sea").

claims.statement: The ceasg lives in sea, rivers and streams; grants three wishes to her captor.
claims.statement_id: Ceasg tinggal di laut, sungai, dan aliran air; mengabulkan tiga permintaan kepada penangkapnya.
claims.quote: The ceasg lives not only in the sea but also in rivers and streams, and can be made to grant three wishes to anyone who captures her.

claims.statement: The ceasg protects her human descendants in storms and guides them to fishing grounds; famous pilots descend from her.
claims.statement_id: Ceasg tetap melindungi keturunan manusianya dari badai dan menuntun ke tempat ikan; pilot ternama keturunannya.
claims.quote: Even when these marriages end and the ceasg returns to the sea, they will always take an interest in their human descendants, protecting them in storms or guiding them to the best fishing grounds.

claims.statement: The hero, swallowed along with his harp-playing wife, on a wizard's advice kills the ceasg by crushing the egg holding her life force.
claims.statement_id: Pahlawan, ditelan bersama istrinya yang bermain harpa, atas nasihat penyihir membunuh ceasg dengan menghancurkan telur berisi daya hidupnya.
claims.quote: He is told that he must obtain a special egg that contains the mermaid's life force. He obtains the egg, rescues his wife, and kills the mermaid by crushing the egg.

claims.statement: Donald MacKenzie suggested the ceasg was once a sea goddess receiving human sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Donald MacKenzie menduga ceasg semula dewi laut penerima korban manusia.
claims.quote: The Scottish folklorist Donald MacKenzie suggested that the ceasg may originally have been a sea goddess to whom human beings were sacrificed.

claims.statement: The ceasg is a mermaid (sereia) of Scottish mythology, half woman and half salmon.
claims.statement_id: Ceasg putri duyung (sereia) mitologi Skotlandia, setengah perempuan setengah salem.
claims.quote: Uma ceasg é uma sereia na mitologia escocesa, uma meia-mulher e um meio-salmonete (salmão) sobrenatural.
